column1: INCOMPLETE GUVNOR REST APIS
column11:
Guvnor is one of the components supporting web tooling for Drools and jBPM. This JIRA project can be used for any issues relating to Drools web tooling.

See http://blog.athico.com/2013/06/goodbye-guvnor-hello-drools-workbench.html for details.
column47:
The "REST" apis exposed in the Guvnor don't adequately cover the functionality required by remote users of the Guvnor.  Guvnor should expose a REST based stack for:

a) creating, deleting, checking-in and checking-out "KnowledgeBases"
b) creating, deleting, checking-in and checking-out "Models" (jars, bpel packages, declarative models)
c) creating, deleting, checking-in and checking-out other resources, such as ruleflows, drools rules (DRLs), rule templates, test scenarios, etc.
d) compiling and creating snapshosts for said knowledgebases and dependencies.

Of this group, creating and checking-in "KnowledgeBases" and allowing compilation of a given knowledgebase and snapshot creation/deploy seems the most important issues.

Basically, David Sotty, Esteban, Mauricio and myself got into a discussion at RulesFest about some remote functionality we'd like to have in the Guvnor, along with a simple Maven plugin that could use these remote methods to add the deployment of resources (java jar "models", drl files, packages, functions, etc.)  and remote "compilation" or "package" creation on the Guvnor itself. After getting back from RulesFest, I emailed Mauricio, Esteban and David to see if any of what looked to be simple changes might be implemented in the Guvnor.  Esteban replied as follows:

>Basically, I saw 2 places where we can expose the functionality you need:
>
>1.- org.drools.guvnor.server.files.PackageDeploymentServlet
>2.- org.drools.guvnor.server.files.RestAPIServlet
>
>The first servlet is used to import a whole DRL file into a guvnor's package. If you want to use it, 
> you must perform a POST action with the following parameters:
>   - "packageName": the name of the package where the DRL is going to be imported. If the package doesn't exist, it is created.
>   - an <input type="file"> with any name: the DRL file.
>
>You can easily modify that servlet to accept an extra parameter to compile the uploaded drl. 
>Here is a code snippet that you can add after the drl is uploaded:
>
>           if(request.getParameter("buildAfterUpload") != null && !request.getParameter("buildAfterUpload").trim().equals("")){
>              ServiceImplementation serv = RepositoryServiceServlet.getService();
>              String packageUUID = serv.getRulesRepository().loadPackage(packageName).getUUID();
>              serv.buildPackage(packageUUID, true);
>           }
>
>The problem here is that if you need a jar model for your rules, the compilation will fail.

He also suggested looking at the REST interface in the Guvnor:

>The second approach seams to be the best way to go. You could expose all the operations you 
>need (like create a package, upload a jar, upload a drl, compile, etc) using REST. RestAPIServlet 
>uses org.drools.repository.remoteapi.RestAPI to perform all its actions. You can use that class as start point.

I've been looking into what REST functionality is exposed in that Servlet and API, to see what further changes might be required.  I've also done some thinking about a class hierarchy from a REST point of view, in terms of the different types of assets that are exposed.  I haven't thought through package compilation, yet, however. Otherwise, I'd gladly consume a fix around these issues and get back to work on my Maven plugin. :)

>Although I'm not sure viewing all content from a package perspective is the best. A rest api where content would be accessible by type, might be nicer. For 
>example:

>/org.drools.guvnor.Guvnor/api/technicalrules/{technicalRuleId}

>An "actions" part of a URL would be useful. For example: 
>
>/org.drools.guvnor.Guvnor/api/packages/{packageName}/compile 
>/org.drools.guvnor.Guvnor/api/technicalrules/{technicalRuleId}/compile 

The breakdown by content-type, with actions available might be a much nicer way to go.  To do this, we'd need another JAX-RS implementation to take the place of the "API" and remove the "ACTIONS" servlet.  I thought a half-step might be useful to start this process, as I wouldn't presume to replace the existing API servlet without some discussion.  :)  

After some thought, I think a solution like the following might be very nice and quite RESTfull:

http://localhost:80/guvnor/packages/{packageName}  -- list the package
http://localhost:80/guvnor/packages/{packageName}/compile -- compile the package
http://localhost:80/guvnor/packages/{packageName}/create-snapshot -- create a snapshot of the package
http://localhost:80/guvnor/packages/{packageName}/snapshot/{snapshotName} -- get the snapshot 

http://localhost:80/guvnor/technicalrules/{technicalRuleId}/compile
http://localhpst:80/guvnor/models/jars/{jarId}

{jarId} and {technicalRuleId} wouldn't be required when accessing via a package:

http://localhost:80/guvnor/packages/{packageName}/models/jars/{jarName}
http://localhost:80/guvnor/packages/{packageName}/technicalrules/{ruleName}

etc.

This would require a bunch of changes to the Guvnor's web.xml.  If I were to do the implementation, I would also need some insight on the security mechanism the Guvnor is using.  The RESTapi class and now the ActionsAPI class are both returning a kind of fake closure which has it's security evaluated. Why isn't authentication external with SEAM as it is for other web applications?  Could an interceptor filter be created to replace this functionality and allow implementation in more straight-forward Java code?  (E.g., code using JAX-RS)?

Those are the questions which came into my head when I started the small Actions implementation and why I went for a small step. What do you think?

column1: Upgrade JCR 1.16.0-CR1 and component dependencies
Be able to intercept and process oauth principal into gatein user according to provider types
column47:
When i register new account with LinkedIn, i see a registration form with random-string username prefilled (see attachment)
It's because LinkedIn does not provide username as unique attribute for each user, so we have to get userid instead of username, and this is a random-string by LinkedIn

Now, We can improvement method OAuthUtils#convertOAuthPrincipalToGateInUser() and customize the way to convert oauth-principal to gatein user for linkedIn.
But when someone provide other oauth integration via extension, he can not customize OAuthUtils#convertOAuthPrincipalToGateInUser() method to generate gatein user by the way that oauth should do.

So we should enable developer change the way to generate gatein user for each oauth provider via extension.

To enable developer change the way to generate gatein user via extension, we will:
- Introduce OAuthUserGenerator service and it can add OAuthUserGeneratorPlugin by extension. This service will response to generate gatein user from oauth-principal
- Method OAuthUserGenerator#generateGateInUser(OAuthPrincipal principal) will do:
  + Find OAuthUserGeneratorPlugin by oauthProviderType, 
  + If found plugin for this oauth provider it will delegate method OAuthUserGeneratorPlugin#generateGateInUser()
  + If not found, it will delegate to OAuthUtils#convertOAuthPrincipalToGateInUser() as default.

column1: Improvements of handling of <priority> in navigation.xml
column47:
This is followup of GTNPORTAL-2751, GTNPORTAL-3324 and GTNPORTAL-3350.

(1) Introduce {{PageNavigation.UNDEFINED_PRIORITY}} constant and use it instead of {{-1}} literal as {{PageNavigation.priority}} value. 

(2) {{UNDEFINED_PRIORITY}} and its usage should be described in comments.

(3) Fix the comparator in [UserPortalImpl|https://github.com/gatein/gatein-portal/blob/master/component/portal/src/main/java/org/exoplatform/portal/mop/user/UserPortalImpl.java#L149] as it does not impose a total ordering as required by the Comparator interface: "The implementor must ensure that sgn(compare(x, y)) == -sgn(compare(y, x)) for all x and y." This does not hold when comparing two nodes both having priority -1.

column1: Change Language Selector changes to default language on save
column47:
The change language selector will change the language to the default on a save if the language value is not changed.

For instance, if the language is not currently the default the change language dialog will open and have the current language selected in the UI. If the user clicks save, instead of the language remaining the same it will default to the portal's default language.
column245:
1) change the language to french
2) open the change language dialog
3) see that french is shown as being selected
4) click save
5) notice that even though the dialog showed french as the selected language, the language is now changed back to english

Note: if you click on the selected french, then it will remain french on save. This only occurs if you open the dialog and click save without clicking on another language.

column1: Warn when a PortalContainerDef contains a non-existent dependency.
column47:
This is important in a situation when a developer works on a Portal Extension or custom portal and he includes a non-existent dependency in the configuration of {{org.exoplatform.container.definition.PortalContainerDefinitionPlugin}} in {{configuration.xml}} file. 

Currently, the portal does not complain at all, the resource loading does not work as expected by the developer but he has little chance to track down the problem quickly and effectively. The portal should definitely warn when {{PortalContainerDefinition}} contains a non-existent dependency.
column277:
27/Sep/13 5:07 AM;vstorm83;portal's dependencies list declared in PortalContainerDefinitionPlugin are use to :

1. Arrange the order of portal container config owner (use last win strategy). Any extension webapp contexts that is NOT in the dependency list will be compared by using it's name.
--> The dependency list is just a configuration and it doesn't depends on webapp deployment. And as I know, we don't support to remove dependency if a webapp is undeployed. I'm not sure we should check those dependenies existent. May be a solution is: Warning if any container config owner (extension webapp) that is not in the dependency list

2. See if a webapp context belong to particular portal container (valid scope) 
--> if ignoreUnregisteredWebapp is set to TRUE, and a webapp context is not in the dep list, it will not be considered valid in that portal container scope --> not allow to add portal init task from that webapp. So we can add a warning to PortalContainerConfig#getPortalContainerNames and PortalContainerConfig#getPortalContainerName method

So we should create a jira on Kernel project for this

column1: Hyphens not allowed in Javascript Modules
Portal keep session alive property values are confusing
column47:
According to documentation, portal "keep seesion alive" property values meaning are as follows:

never - The session will never timeout, even if an application requests it.
On-demand - The session will timeout if an application requests it
Always - The session will time out after a set period

This is quite confusing. E.g. keep session alive never actually means to keep session alive forever.

Keep session alive always means to let the session timeout automatically.


If the documentation is correct, the name of the property or property values should be changed.

* Explicitly state in the documentation [1] that {{<priority>}} is considered only if not already set (first wins).

h3. Solution Proposal B
* Make {{<priority>}} optional in {{gatein_objects}} XSD and  {{NavigationMarshaller.unmarshalNavigation(StaxNavigator<Element>)}}
* Change the behavior of {{NavigationMarshaller.unmarshalNavigation(StaxNavigator<Element>)}} to the effect that {{<priority>}} is handled in the same way as navigation nodes: it is used or ignored according to the chosen {{importMode}}. Esp. for {{importMode}} {{merge}} the last read {{<priority>}} should win.
* Document it in [1]

For both A and B the most or all occutences of {{<priority>}} should be removed from Portal Extension Quickstart.

[1] [https://docs.jboss.org/author/display/GTNPORTAL35/Portal+Navigation+Configuration]

column1: Externalize default-repository in JCR configuration
column47:
Variablize default-repository and repository's name in Repository Service configuration, to make possible repository name configuration via configuration.properties.
Usage of the variable should be as follows:
{code}
<repository-service default-repository="${gatein.jcr.repository.default}">
  <repositories>
    <repository name="${gatein.jcr.repository.default}" system-workspace="${gatein.jcr.workspace.system}" default-workspace="${gatein.jcr.workspace.default}">
      ...
    </repository>
  </repositories>
</repository-service>
{code}

The configuration.properties will be:
{code}
# JCR system and default workspaces
gatein.jcr.repository.default=repository
gatein.jcr.workspace.default=collaboration
gatein.jcr.workspace.system=system

column280:

column1: actionScopedRequestAttributes not available for portlets
column47:
javax.portlet.actionScopedRequestAttributes do not seem to be functioning.

This blog post descibes what it should do:

http://wpcertification.blogspot.com/2011/02/actionscopedrequestattributes-container.html

They make possible to call request.setAttribute() from processAction() to RenderRequest, to be available in the PortletFilter.

There is a workaround by using response.setRenderParameter(), but I have a portlet that is already working in Liferay and I'd like to port it to GateIn by having this feature available.

I have this in my portlet.xml:

  <container-runtime-option>
       <name>javax.portlet.actionScopedRequestAttributes</name> 
       <value>true</value> 
  </container-runtime-option>

Still those attributes I set in processAction get lost, and are not available by RenderRequest.getAttribute()

column1: Portlet's context-root cannot contain slashes
column47:
I've tried to use a context-root with a slash "/" in a JSR-286 Hello World Portlet and it throws the following exception when trying to add it to a new page:

11:59:46,926 ERROR [STDERR] org.gatein.pc.api.NoSuchPortletException: No such portlet /oag.ade
11:59:46,926 ERROR [STDERR] at org.gatein.pc.portlet.container.ContainerPortletInvoker.getPortlet(ContainerPortletInvoker.java:99)

Changing context-root to not contain slashes has fixed the problem.

Problem happens when using slashes "/" in:

application.xml of an .ear file
<module>
<web>
<web-uri>seamBookingPortlet.war</web-uri>
<context-root>/oag/ade</context-root>
</web>
</module>
Changing it to <context-root>/oag-ade</context-root> fixes the problem

jboss-web.xml of a .war file
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<jboss-web>
<context-root>/LG_1648_1_WEB/SamplePortlet</context-root>
</jboss-web>
Changing it to <context-root>/LG_1648_1_WEB.SamplePortlet</context-root> fixes the problem.

15/Feb/11 11:42 AM;julien_viet;I have modified the unit test to check that behavior and it actually does not happen, here is in short what the unit test does (among other things): it involves two portlet UTP1 and UTP2

step 1 : UTP1 renders markup and set validity for 2 seconds, UTP2 ask the test controller to show the next page as a resource
step 2 : UTP2 is displayed as a resource and does not involve UTP1, it performs a 1 second pause and ask the controller to show a render page that will involve both portlets
step 3 : UTP2 renders and UTP1 should not be rendered (UTP1 set a cached boolean to false to assert it later), UTP2 ask the test controller to display again a resource
step 4 : UTP2 resource rendering occurs it performs a one second pause and ask the controller to render the full page

column277:
16/Apr/10 6:24 AM;hoang_to;That issue comes from a wrong usage of filtered navigation on UITree.

1. The UITree is aimed to represent a certain navigation N

2. The navigation N is firstly filtered and become N' ( as we need to hide some node from navigation N)

3. The UITree object is instantiated with navigation N'

4. Once the data in UITree object is persisted, navigation N' would replace navigation N


That cause node missing ( for deletable node) or changes in node order

Solution:

- UITree object hold a reference to orginial navigation N, persistence actions is done with N

- UITree hold a reference to a boolean tree structure ( or simply N') to manage node displaying
column278:
28/Apr/10 10:33 PM;hoang_to;Currently, the tree node used in the component is the default UITree in the framework, which does not allow the node displaying management based on input data ( see GTNPORTAL-1139). Therefore, we attempted the 'synchronizing' approach.

   Original and filtered navigations are kept in UINodeNavigationSelector, filtered one is parsed to UITree, and original one is used for persistence. Changes come from filtred navigation is propagated to original navigation.  This approach is complex and buggy, especially in the case a node is moved UP/DOWN, that usually results in intolerable page node order

column1: soTimeout option is used by SFTP of camel-ftp
column47:
According to the document(1), `soTimeout` is used only for `FTP and FTPS`, not SFTP.
However, as long as I read the source code(2), `soTimeout` is used for `Session.setTimeout()`(3) of SFTP. I guess this is a documentation bug. 

The source code(2) was fixed by CAMEL-8757(4). I think the modification of the document was missed when to fix.

By the way, our community document(5) is also not correct. 

(1) Fuse Document
    https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_fuse/6.3/html-single/apache_camel_component_reference/#IDU-FTP2
~~~
- connectTimeout
-- Camel 2.4: Is the connect timeout in millis. This corresponds to using ftpClient.connectTimeout for the FTP/FTPS. For SFTP this option is also used when attempting to connect.
- soTimeout
-- FTP and FTPS Only:Camel 2.4: Is the SocketOptions.SO_TIMEOUT value in millis.
- timeout
-- FTP and FTPS Only:Camel 2.4: Is the data timeout in millis. This corresponds to using ftpClient.dataTimeout for the FTP/FTPS. For SFTP there is no data timeout.
~~~

(2) org/apache/camel/component/file/remote/SftpOperations.java
{code:java}
        // set the SO_TIMEOUT for the time after the connect phase
         if (configuration.getSoTimeout() > 0) {
             session.setTimeout(configuration.getSoTimeout());
         }
{code}

(3) com.jcraft.jsch.Session Java Doc 
    https://epaul.github.io/jsch-documentation/simple.javadoc/com/jcraft/jsch/Session.html#setTimeout-int-
~~~
sets the timeout setting. This value is used as the socket timeout parameter, and also as the default connection timeout.
~~~

(4) [CAMEL-8757] SO_TIMEOUT not really set on SFTP connections
  - https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-8757

(5) Community Document
http://people.apache.org/~dkulp/camel/ftp2.html
~~~
- connectTimeout	
-- Camel 2.4: Is the connect timeout in millis. This corresponds to using ftpClient.connectTimeout for the FTP/FTPS. For SFTP this option is also used when attempting to connect.
- soTimeout	
-- FTP and FTPS Only: Camel 2.4: Is the SocketOptions.SO_TIMEOUT value in millis. Note SFTP will automatic use the connectTimeout as the soTimeout.
- timeout	
-- FTP and FTPS Only: Camel 2.4: Is the data timeout in millis. This corresponds to using ftpClient.dataTimeout for the FTP/FTPS. For SFTP there is no data timeout.
~~~

column1: Configuration to securely access maven repository using basic authentication in fabric environment.
column47:
- We have a better solution for problem described in description section of JIRA  [ENTESB-7425|https://issues.jboss.org/browse/ENTESB-7425]
- In documentation we can add
*Securely access maven repository in Fabric environment.*

 There is template versions of both:
* maven-settings.xml
* maven-settings-security.xml

in default profile. Additionally, these files are actually copied to etc/ when container joins fabric, so now it's just a matter of changing these files in default profile (in hawtio for example) and the changes will be propagated to all containers.

There's also new shell command: fabric:maven-password. By default, it prints Maven security settings - it checks all Maven configurations (explicit and implicit) and prints the status, for example:

{noformat}
JBossFuse:karaf@root> fabric:maven-password 
Maven security configuration in Fabric environment defined in io.fabric8.maven and io.fabric8.agent PID.
  Security settings file: /data/servers/jboss-fuse-6.3.0.redhat-311/etc/maven-settings-security.xml
  Encrypted Maven master password: {PMFs1x/vuOMHhjzIZpzst/d5Kpna+WqNu3P15ZcIP8g=}
JBossFuse:karaf@root> fabric:maven-password -d
Maven security configuration in Fabric environment defined in io.fabric8.maven and io.fabric8.agent PID.
  Security settings file: /data/servers/jboss-fuse-6.3.0.redhat-311/etc/maven-settings-security.xml
  Decrypted Maven master password: fabric:changeit
{noformat}

{{-d}} - decrypts master Maven password found in security settings.

There are also two additional options to encrypt Maven passwords:
{{--encrypt-master-password/-emp}} - encrypts master Maven password, which should be *manually* added to current settings-security.xml file. Why manually? Because it's used to decrypt ordinary passwords that *may* be now in use. So user has to be conscious about what he/she's doing.

{noformat}
JBossFuse:karaf@root> fabric:maven-password --encrypt-master-password 
Master Maven password: 
Verify master Maven password: 
Encrypted master Maven password to use in security-settings.xml: {94gq/tbm0IYHZl4M6BstgfnY/iErAy+GKlfXiptLL/Q=}
{noformat}

{{--ecnrypt-password}}/{{-ep}} - encrypts ordinary Maven password, to be used for server and http proxy authentication configuration. It *requires* configured master Maven password. For example:

{noformat}
JBossFuse:karaf@root> fabric:maven-password --encrypt-password 
Looking up master Maven password in /data/servers/jboss-fuse-6.3.0.redhat-311/etc/maven-settings-security.xml... Done!
Maven password: 
Verify Maven password: 
Encrypted Maven password to use in settings.xml for server and proxy authentication: {WCUxIVlatO4HZG2xrqtVBziJIeDTTuVK1oCNEA2eKEQ=}
{noformat}

There's also one _quirk_. If you modify one of the above files inside {{default}} profile, there'll be *no* automatic reload of these files - that's how the profiles work. Only PID configuration changes lead to restart of related SCR components or blueprint containers. So in order to pick up the changes you have to:
* refresh {{default}} profile, so fabric-agent will use changed configuration
* restart {{fabric-maven}} bundle to make changes available for {{mvn:}} URI handler and {{fabric-maven-proxy}}

 *If we summarize following configuration has to modifed:*

 - User has to configure  io.fabric8.agent.properties/org.ops4j.pax.url.mvn.repositories in default profile as:
{noformat}
org.ops4j.pax.url.mvn.repositories= http://localhost:8081/repository/maven-releases@id=nexus
{noformat}

- Than he needs to edit settings.xml for server authentication with maven-password as created above.
{code:xml}  
<servers>
    <server>
        <id>nexus</id>
        <username>developer</username>
        <password>{ROfEzDmC46kHzzXhLbVCRImwa5tXZFG+33PvGCnFLUg=}</password>
    </server>
    -----
</servers>
{code}

 - At last edit security-settings.xml in default profile with content like:
{code:xml}
<settingsSecurity>
  <master>{fvmX0OzPBaAHqgEMK6xjlJSh4frQNL5E5zxbV8vyTWo=}</master>
</settingsSecurity>
{code}

column1: Merge FSW Development Guides into the Fuse Repo
column47:
As a first step in the merge of the Fuse and FSW docs suites, we need to merge the Development Guides into the Fuse repo.

This involves the following books, and they should be renamed as outlined below: 

Development_Guide_Volume_1_SwitchYard -> SwitchYard Development Guide
Development_Guide_Volume_2_Smooks -> Smooks Development Guide
Development_Guide_Volume_3_Governance -> Governance Development Guide
Development_Guide_Volume_4_BPEL -> BPEL Development Guide

Please rename both the book's directory and the actual name in the book's master file.

The merged books need to be structured in the Sibin format, not the standard Publican format. That means:

- contents of the en-US directory should go right under the book's main directory
- the <book name>.xml file should follow the same format as other books in the Fuse repo; extra entries need to be taken from the Book_Info.xml and Author_Group.xml files

Entries for the added books also need to be added to the sibin.cfg file in the root of the repo.

This work should be done in the master branch of the Fuse repo.

07/Sep/15 9:39 PM;nmoore;Here are the scripts Petr provided, and the main processes I followed to get this done. 
From the FUSEDOC-xxx branch
Copy ~/fswdocs/Development_Guide_Volume_1_SwitchYard/en_US SwitchYard_Development_Guide
Edit the Development_Guide_Volume_1_SwitchYard.xml guide to include the <info> section as shown in the .xml files for the other books. If you don't do this there will be a Sibin error.
Run the following scripts:
To get rid of the Bugzilla links:

sed -i '/<para role="RoleCreateBugPara">/,+2d' topics/**/**

sed -i '/<para role="RoleCreateBugPara">/,+2d' *.xml

n.b. This may not pick up all of them. You'll have to remove some manually when you come across them. 

To get rid of entity definitions in the header of chapter files:
sed -i 's/Development_Guide_Volume_1_SwitchYard.ent/..\/Library.ent/g' *.xml

n.b. Replace Development_Guide_Volume_1_SwitchYard.en in the command to reflect the current book name. 

To replace <xi:include>s that reference individual topic files with their actual content, use this command:

for i in ./chap-*.xml; do mv "$i" "$i.bak" || exit 1 && xmllint --xinclude "$i.bak" > "$i" && rm "$i.bak";done

From Book_Info.xml, remove the "id" attribute on the <book> element, otherwise the book can't be built. E.g.

<bookinfo id="book-Development_Guide_Volume_1_SwitchYard-Development_Guide_Volume_1_SwitchYard">
->
<bookinfo>


Many of the chap-*.xml files have entity names in them. They need to be removed. Start under the 

%BOOK_ENTITIES;
]>

line and remove all the variable definitions up to the <book> tag.

In the Bookname_Development_Guide.xml file, remove the Book_Info.xml line and the Preface.xml line. They will cause problems in the Sibin gen and aren't needed for this brand.

Update sibin.cfg to include the book you're working on.

column1: add the doc for org.apache.karaf.jaas.modules.properties.AutoEncryptionSupport  in "Encrypting Stored Passwords" section"
column47:
In  JBoss FUSE 6.2 we introduce a org.apache.karaf.jaas.modules.properties.AutoEncryptionSupport class to automatically encrypt the passwords in users.properties without login if users configure the jaas realm to enable the encryption. So in "Encrypting Stored Passwords" section, besides the encryption properties in <jaas:module...,  aslo need add AutoEncryptionSupport bean configuration like
{code}
<bean class="org.apache.karaf.jaas.modules.properties.AutoEncryptionSupport"
            init-method="init" destroy-method="destroy">
        <argument>
            <map>
                <entry key="org.osgi.framework.BundleContext" value-ref="blueprintBundleContext"/>
                <entry key="users" value="$[karaf.base]/etc/users.properties"/>
                <entry key="encryption.name" value="jasypt"/>
                <entry key="encryption.enabled" value="true"/>
                <entry key="encryption.prefix" value="{CRYPT}"/>
                <entry key="encryption.suffix" value="{CRYPT}"/>
                <entry key="encryption.algorithm" value="SHA-256"/>
                <entry key="encryption.encoding" value="base64"/>
                <entry key="encryption.iterations" value="100000"/>
                <entry key="encryption.saltSizeBytes" value="16"/>
            </map>
        </argument>
    </bean>
{code}

DESCRIPTION
        fabric:profile-edit

	Edits the specified version of the specified profile (where the version defaults to the current default version)

SYNTAX
        fabric:profile-edit [options] profile [version] 

ARGUMENTS
        profile
                The target profile to edit
        version
                The version of the profile to edit. Defaults to the current default version.

OPTIONS
        -i, --import-pid
                Imports the pids that are edited, from local OSGi config admin
        --help
                Display this help message

                Specifies the delimiter to use for appends and removals.

                Edit overrides, specifying a comma-separated list of overrides to add (or delete).
        -r, --repositories
                Edit the features repositories
        -p, --pid
                Edit an OSGi configuration property, specified in the format <PID>/<Property>.
        --resource
                Selects a resource under the profile to edit. This option should only be used alone.
        -f, --features
                Edit features, specifying a comma-separated list of features to add (or delete).
        --remove
                Removes value from a delimited list. It is only usable with the system, config & pid options
        --set
                Set or create values (selected by default).
                (defaults to true)
        --append
                Append value to a delimited list. It is only usable with the system, config & pid options
        --fabs
                Edit fabs, specifying a comma-separated list of fabs to add (or delete).
        -n, --endorsed
                Edit endorsed libraries, specifying a comma-separated list of libs to add (or delete).
        -b, --bundles
                Edit bundles, specifying a comma-separated list of bundles to add (or delete).
        -s, --system
                Edit the Java system properties that affect installed bundles (analogous to editing etc/system.properties in a root container).
        -l, --libs
                Edit libraries, specifying a comma-separated list of libs to add (or delete).
        -c, --config
                Edit the Java system properties that affect the karaf container (analogous to editing etc/config.properties in a root container).
        -x, --extension
                Edit extension libraries, specifying a comma-separated list of libs to add (or delete).

column47:
Steps to reproduce :
1. Login as *admin*, create node */node1*
2. Remove all permission for *any*
3. Add for *john* permissions *READ*, *SET_PROPERTY* and *REMOVE*
4. Login as *john* and try to add a *mixin* for this node
Exception: 
{code:title=Exception}
javax.jcr.AccessDeniedException: Access denied: ADD_NODE or SET_PROPERTY[]:1[]node1:1 for: john item owner __system" type="junit.framework.AssertionFailedError">junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: javax.jcr.AccessDeniedException: Access denied: ADD_NODE or SET_PROPERTY[]:1[]node1:1 for: john item owner __system
{code}
Link: [https://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/ECMS-3545]
column277: 16/Mar/12 4:40 AM;nfilotto;This is a normal behavior, to add a mixin type you need both SET_PROPERTY and ADD_NODE permissions
column278:
19/Mar/12 10:04 PM;minh_dang;Hi Nicolas,

Could you explain more details on this? We need to explain more clearly with reporter.

Thanks,
Minh
column279: 20/Mar/12 4:24 AM;nfilotto;To allow a user to add a mixin to a given node the JCR checks if it has the permissions SET_PROPERTY and ADD_NODE on that particular node. In other words addMixin is a special operation that requires special rights. In this particular case john doesn't have the permission ADD_NODE so it fails which is a normal behavior as it is mandatory. BTW why do you consider it as a bug?
column280: 21/Mar/12 11:28 PM;anhvurz90;As I understand, to add a mixin to a given node, we just need to change the property *jcr:mixinTypes*. So only permision *SET_PROPERTY* is enough. Why you require user to have permission *ADD_NODE*?
column281:
22/Mar/12 3:03 AM;tolusha;Because of this: some mixins can contain auto-created nodes and properties.
And in general case we should have both permissions: SET_PROPERTY and ADD_NODE
column282:
26/Mar/12 12:03 AM;anhvurz90;@Nicolas Filotto, Anatoliy Bazko:
In our scenario, as you read in [https://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/ECMS-3545], user does not care about the *addMixin* funtion. He just notices that he has *SET_PROPERTY* and *REMOVE* permissions but can not edit the document. The question here is:
- Do we need the *ADD_NODE* permission for all cases of *addMixin*? I think we only need it when the *mixin* node type contains at least 1 mandatory auto-created nodes. In case it does not have these things, *ADD_NODE* is not necessary.
column283: 26/Mar/12 4:18 AM;nfilotto;In anyway this can be considered as a bug, at best it could be considered as an improvement but as 1.14 is already in maintenance mode it is too late now for an improvement, which means that it could be done in JCR 1.15. In your use case, I personally don't consider it as a bug, he wants to edit a doc and to do so you need RW access to it
column284:
26/Mar/12 4:43 AM;minh_dang;Hi Nicolas,

IMO, that is a real use case in WCM and in the real life. He wants to edit a document so he just has edit permission on it. Why do we need *Add* permission? is it safe to let people has more permission than what he has to do? It is not logical for me.
And if you consider this one could be done in JCR 1.15 then could you reopen it and add into 1.15 scope? 

Thanks,
Minh
column285:
26/Mar/12 5:15 AM;nfilotto;>> Why do we need Add permission? is it safe to let people has more permission than what he has to do? It is not logical for me.
<< Maybe it is not logical but it is how it works from the beginning so changing it now would be a behavior change which is forbidden in a maintenance branch as you know

>> And if you consider this one could be done in JCR 1.15 then could you reopen it and add into 1.15 scope? 
<< Done

BTW: The given unit test cannot work even with this improvement as making a node mix:versionable will add nodes to create the history of this node, so I guess it should be replaced with something like mix:lockable which seems to be the current issue in ECMS-3545
column286:
26/Mar/12 7:27 AM;benjamin.paillereau;I would agree with Nico. We always had this behaviour. AFAIK, it has never been a problem.

Plus, feature speaking, we should merge "SET_PROPERTY" and "ADD_NODE" as one permission in ECMS. Those go together in most cases.
column287: 30/Mar/12 1:06 PM;nfilotto;The goal of this task will be to improve the jcr in order to make it check the permission ADD_NODE only if it had to add nodes automatically when the mixin type has been added
column288: 05/Apr/12 4:13 AM;anhvurz90;Hi all. There is another case similar to this issue. That is when user has *ADD_NODE* permission but he can not add child node to the node. *JCR* requires both *ADD_NODE* and *SET_PROPERTY*. What about your idea? Attachment: [^TestAddNodePermission.java]
column289: 05/Apr/12 4:39 AM;nfilotto;If the user has *ADD_NODE* permission on a node, he can add child nodes to this node so your use case makes no sense at all

column293: 05/Apr/12 5:03 AM;nfilotto;That is totally normal, the access permissions of node11 are inherited from node1 which are PermissionType.READ and PermissionType.ADD_NODE and SET_PROPERTY permission is mandatory when you add a mixin type even with this improvement since when we add a mixin type we modify the property jcr:mixinTypes
column294: 05/Apr/12 5:16 AM;anhvurz90;Although user only has permissions *READ* and *ADD_NODE* for parent node, he is the creator of the child node, so he should have ALL permission with the child node. It makes more sence
column295: 05/Apr/12 5:28 AM;nfilotto;According to your error message the owner is not john but __system so your assumption is incorrect

The owner is not set automatically when you add a node, you need to add the mixin type "exo:owneable" to have it set
column298:

column1: Write a guide that explains how to fix a corrupted JCR
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
The goal of this task is to write a guide that will describe what to do in case of a corrupted JCR. The first thing to do, is to identify all the potential cause of a consistency issue, here are some of them:
* An item is its own parent which causes an infinite loop if we try to create the path
* A node that doesn't have any properties/primary type
* A node that has a single valued properties with nothing declared in the VALUE table knowing that the missing property could be the primary type
* An item that doesn't have any parent node
* A node that is considered as locked in the lockmanager data but not in the jcr data or the opposite
* A property which value is stored in the File System but its content is missing
... 
All the queries launched by the consistency checker should be covered by this guide, users need to know what to do in case one of the queries returns some results

Some part of the guide can be extracted from this conversation based on real life use case https://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/SPREDHAT-122

column1: Allow to have dedicated tables per workspace even in single db mode
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47: The goal of this task is to split the data of each workspace in a dedicated tables even in single db mode. Indeed in practice only the single db mode is used by the customer which has for consequences to have all the data of all the workspaces in the same tables which cause perf issues when we have a lot of data. As the size of the table grows very quickly, it is critical to slip the data to be able to have several medium tables instead of one huge. So we need to add a new sub class of JDBCWorkspaceDataContainer that will store the data in tables of the same structure as the current multi db mode for both mode, the only difference is the fact that the table names are now dynamic and will be composed of the workspace name, the tables could then be of type JCRI_${escaped_workspace_name} for the ITEM table, JCRV_${escaped_workspace_name} for the VALUE table and JCRR_${escaped_workspace_name} for the REF table. In case the name of the workspace is too long, we can add a new parameter in the config allow to set a short workspace name that will be used instead of the workspace name.

column47:
I am using the MailService in my code to create some notifications.

The send message operation it taking lot of time, it would be great to provide in our API a way to send service asynchronously and let the service deals in a performant way (queuing messages for example)
column277: 03/Feb/12 10:14 AM;nfilotto;That makes perfect sense, thx for the feedback
column278:
03/Feb/12 10:38 AM;nfilotto;To do this new feature, I propose to add 3 new methods to the MailService interface that will be sendMessageInFuture (one for each sendMessage method). These new method won't throw any Exception and instead will return a Future<Boolean>. In case the message has been properly send, _future.get()_ will return true otherwise the exception could be get from the ExecutionException. In other words sendMessageInFuture(...) will send the message asynchronously so if we want to have a callback we need to use the returned Future object such that if we call future.get() the message will be send asynchronously be the calling thread will wait until the message is sent so it would be equivalent to sendMessage(..) except the fact that the messages are sent by a pool instead of the calling thread which is more scalable.

In MailServiceImpl as implementation of Future, we can simply use _FutureTask_ that we will put into an _ExecutorService_ created from _Executors.newFixedThreadPool(int nThreads, ThreadFactory threadFactory)_ where nThreads will be a new parameter in the configuration by default the value will be _Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors()_ and threadFactory will be set such that we will have an explicit name for the related threads.

NB: In the context of this issue please add some javadoc to the MailService interface

column1: Ensure that all the running transactions are over before allowing to stop the JCR
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
The goal of this task is to ensure that if when we have a JCR running with updates in progress and the administrator calls Ctrl + C to properly stop the server, we need to be sure that the running transactions are over before stopping the JCR otherwise it could create some inconsistency between for example the JCR data and the Lock Data and/or the luncene indexes. I checked by adding a pause at the beginning and at the end of the method CacheableWorkspaceDataManager.doSave(), these pauses are added on demand only to allow the server to start, I built a JCR on tomcat, I launched the server, added some content using FTP and realized that when I call Ctrl + C, the workspace is stopped even if there is a tx running. 

The proposed patch simply suspends the workspace at CacheableWorkspaceDataManager.stop() which ensures that no new updates will be allowed and the running ones will be completed before stopping the workspace.

column47:
Running eXo JCR with DB2 requires to have the following setting:
DB2_COMPATIBILITY_VECTOR=MYS
Which allows to use LIMIT and OFFSET keywords.

This setting is enabled by default in certain versions of DB2 but not all.

The more recommended way for DB2 is to use the RAW_NEXT OLAP function as stated here:
http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/data/library/techarticle/0307balani/0307balani.html

If you fail to do so, EPP would not start (Fails during indexing)

column1: Parallel text extractions doesn't work with clustered index strategies
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Usecase is the following:
- There is a save() containing multiple structured documents (like PDF, ODT and ect);
- When saving into index, JCR creates a thread pool executor, that extracts text from documents in parallel.

But, when replicated volatile index was introduced, features stopped working. Root of it is a serialization of Lucene Documents. The last one retrieves the content of Lucene Documents invoking text extraction. This cycle performed before Lucene Document is being placed into index, before thread pool executor used. So there is no performance increase made by thread pool.

column47: Introduce ready-to-use implementation of RSYNC-based index replication.
column277:
18/Jan/12 7:27 AM;nzamosenchuk;h1. Requirements
JCR require configured and launched RSync Server on each cluster node with access via rsync:// protocol.

h1. What implemented
* sync indexes when volatile flushed, both non-system and system;
* sync indexes on cluster node startup, both new and previously re-started node;
* specifying RSync configuration for QueryHandler;
* support of RSync Authentication;

h1. How implemented
Standard Shared Index strategy has much in common with new RSync-Based concept. Only difference is an RSync call when indexes changed on coordinator for synchronization with other cluster nodes. That's why RSync concept is implemented on the top existing JBossCache-based components. JBossCacheIndexChangesFilter updated to handle new type of IndexInfos, RSyncIndexInfos. Those are the classes that manage the list of indexes, calling MultiIndex when list changed. RSyncIndexInfos triggers call to system utility in order to retrieve the last snapshot of index folder. When process finished, then control flow returned to JBossCache-based index components. Also RSync utility invoked on startup to retrieve latest index state.
h1. What tested
Concept launched on 2 and 3-nodes cluster. Following features tested manually:
* basic index synchronization, when coordinator flushes new index;
* index retrieval on startup, when no local index present;
* index re-synchronization on startup, when local index already present;
* coordinator changes;
* temporary outage of some cluster node.
On each step new document was uploaded via Dav and tested launching queries on each node.

Next task is a performance testing, comparing different approaches.
h1. How to configure
You need ordinary JBossCache index configuration as shown below:
{code}
<query-handler class="org.exoplatform.services.jcr.impl.core.query.lucene.SearchIndex">
  <properties>
    <property name="index-dir" value="${exo.jcr.parent.dir:..}/temp/jcrlucenedb/production" />
    <property name="changesfilter-class"
  value="org.exoplatform.services.jcr.impl.core.query.jbosscache.JBossCacheIndexChangesFilter" />
    <property name="jbosscache-configuration" value="jar:/conf/portal/cluster/jbosscache-indexer.xml" />
    <property name="jgroups-configuration" value="jar:/conf/portal/cluster/udp-mux.xml" />
    <property name="jgroups-multiplexer-stack" value="false" />
    <property name="jbosscache-cluster-name" value="JCR-cluster-indexer" />
    <property name="jbosscache-shareable" value="true" />
    <property name="max-volatile-time" value="60" /> 
  </properties>
</query-handler>
{code}
Make sure "index-dir" is pointing to local folder. Then need to add RSync configuration options:
{code}
<query-handler class="org.exoplatform.services.jcr.impl.core.query.lucene.SearchIndex">
  <properties>
    <property name="index-dir" value="${exo.jcr.parent.dir:..}/temp/jcrlucenedb/production" />
    <property name="changesfilter-class"
  value="org.exoplatform.services.jcr.impl.core.query.jbosscache.JBossCacheIndexChangesFilter" />
    <property name="jbosscache-configuration" value="jar:/conf/portal/cluster/jbosscache-indexer.xml" />
    <property name="jgroups-configuration" value="jar:/conf/portal/cluster/udp-mux.xml" />
    <property name="jgroups-multiplexer-stack" value="false" />
    <property name="jbosscache-cluster-name" value="JCR-cluster-indexer" />
    <property name="jbosscache-shareable" value="true" />
    <property name="max-volatile-time" value="60" /> 
    <property name="rsync-entry-name" value="index" />
    <property name="rsync-entry-path" value="/home/exo/tomcat" />
    <property name="rsync-port" value="8085" />
    <property name="rsync-user" value="rsyncexo" />
    <property name="rsync-password" value="exo" />
  </properties>
</query-handler>
{code}

Let's start with authentication: "rsync-user" and "rsync-password". It is optional and can be missing if RSync Server allows anonymous access. Before reviewing other RSync index options need to have a look at RSync server configuration.

Sample RSync Server (rsyncd) Configuration
{code}
uid = nobody
gid = nobody
use chroot = no
port = 8085
log file = rsyncd.log
pid file = rsyncd.pid
[index]
        path = /home/exo/tomcat
        comment = indexes
        read only = true
        auth users = rsyncexo
        secrets file= rsyncd.secrets
{code}
This sample configuration shows entry "index" configured for /home/exo/tomcat folder. This configuration is represented in JCR configuration within "rsync-entry-name", "rsync-entry-path", "rsync-port" properties.

h1. Issues
# Consider using JNI and native lib instead of calling system utility.
# Failover, when coordinator leaves during synchronization. This usecase can break the index.

column47:
Redhat.com is currently migrating on EPP SP, and accenture has done lot of work around performance and scalability testing

During this work they have tested some configuration of the JCR to improve performances :

------
We are continuing to look at the results, and we may have some suggestions for significant improvement. One example is the bottleneck we encountered in the testing (in the graphs - it is when the response times initially jump up to very high levels). Anil (our DBA) has some recommendations to change the way we are querying the database to reduce the amount of time the app spends in filesort - which seemed to be our major bottleneck during the last test (see attached email). Would you like me to open a support ticket to track that? Obviously it is not a critical issue - but if we can make the product even faster, that would be good for everyone.
------

You can find the number regarding DB access below, from aproddut@redhat.com (Anil)


One other option which does not need us to change our order of results is use the following query which contains all the columns in the order by clause ..

select * from JCR_SITEM where CONTAINER_NAME='collaboration' and PARENT_ID='collaboration82ebbeff0a070dbf07bac04c4fc376a7' and NAME='[http://www.exoplatform.com/jcr/exo/1.0]workspace' and I_INDEX=1 order by I_CLASS, VERSION,I_INDEX,NAME,PARENT_ID,CONTAINER_NAME DESC
I guess it would return the same output but the above option will not use filesort.

The current query which application executes is ..

column280:
05/Jan/12 4:08 AM;nfilotto;Please note that the queries are not exactly the same as the original one does an descending sort on the field version and the proposed query does an ascending sort. It seems that removing the "DESC" keyword from the original query is enough to make the filesort disappear. We need to investigate to know if we can remove it but at first glance it seems to be correct as we cannot have 2 different items with the same CONTAINER_NAME, PARENT_ID, NAME, I_INDEX, I_CLASS and with a different version. But anyway if we realize that it is ok on MySQL, we will need to investigate on other DB to know if it will be a change specific to MySQL or a global change.

BTW do we agree that you expect a fix on JCR 1.14 only?
column281:
05/Jan/12 4:25 AM;nfilotto;I finally found the root cause of this unexpected filesort, we expect this query to use the following index "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX JCR_IDX_SITEM_PARENT ON JCR_SITEM(CONTAINER_NAME, PARENT_ID, NAME, I_INDEX, I_CLASS, VERSION DESC);" but according to the doc the keyword DESC is simply ignored by MySQL, I quote "An index_col_name specification can end with ASC or DESC. These keywords are permitted for future extensions for specifying ascending or descending index value storage. Currently, they are parsed but ignored; index values are always stored in ascending order." (more details here http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.5/en/create-index.html)

We need to identify other configurations if they exist that don't support this keyword.
column282: 05/Jan/12 4:39 AM;nfilotto;I checked the doc of DB2, Sybase, Oracle, PGSQL and MSSQL, and none of them mention the fact that it is not supported so the fix should only be applied in case of MySQL

column1: Provide a migration tool for the JCR locks stored in JBoss Cache
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Up to now, there are several things in JCR 1.14 that make impossible to migrate the JCR Locks stored in JBC with a cache loader from 1.12 to 1.14
# Even if we use the exact same config of the lock manager in JCR 1.14 as in JCR 1.12, it cannot work because the root node is always the unique name of the workspace, it should be the case only when the cache is shareable
# When the cache is shareable the root node is the unique name of the workspace to prevent conflicts between the cache instances, which is not compatible with the old data as it doesn't share the same root node and the data is split into different tables

We need to find the easiest way to fix both issues, the first one could be fixed by simply adding the unique name of the workspace only in case the cache is not shareable. The second issue could be fixed by removing the locks from the JCR Tables, in order to be able to safely drop the old tables of JBC and start from a new one that will be the one for the shareable caches. As the proposal for the second issue will need manual tasks like dropping the old tables, it must be well documented.
column277:

But if I understand it correctly, these tables will be empty then (because locks will be removed) and so it should not be a problem for migration ? Only thing is that customers will have empty tables for old locks but I guess this should not be a problem (only few useless additional tables). Is it correct?

Especially I wanted to know if customers will be able to upgrade to shareable without doing any manual steps with their DB (aka deleting old lock tables).

And can we assume that this can be fixed in JCR 1.14.3 (Sorry for bothering, but 1.14.3 is the version, which will be used in EPP 5.2.0.GA) ?

Thanks a lot!

You can see the changes by doing the following diff:

svn diff -r 7504:7557 http://anonsvn.jboss.org/repos/gatein/sandbox/as7_support/branches/gatein-as7/exo.kernel.container/src

Also, there is no custom JMX MBeanServerImpl in JBoss AS7, which using current code produces error level logs even though exceptions are actually ignored.

Create a document in a dms-system workspace
delete it => we see in the log that the listner is triggered

column1: Lucene indexes synchronization based on rsynch command
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Up to now we support 2 different topologies which are:
# Shared indexes on a shared FS with only the coordinator in RW mode the rest of the cluster is in RO mode
# Dedicated indexes for each node and they are all in RW mode

The problem with the first topology is the fact that we need a shared file system which affects the performances and the problem with the second topology is the resynchronization of a node that left the cluster during a certain period of time which can be long especially with a lot of data since we do a full recovery instead of an incremental one.

It could be interesting to propose a mix of both topologies where we will have dedicated indexes for each node but only the coordinator would be in RW mode. When a cluster modify a JCR Node, it builds the corresponding lucene doc and give it to the coordinator, the coordinator adds it to its volatile index and when it persists the volatile index, it triggers an rsynch command. This way the indexes of all the nodes of the cluster will be up to date. Moreover when a node has left the cluster during a period of time and goes back to the cluster, if the corresponding machine was still up (I mean only AS was down) during this period of time the indexes will be up to date otherwise they will be at the next rsynch triggered by the coordinator

An interesting link about the rsynch command http://www.xelon.it/articles/rsync-mac-linux-windows/

10/Nov/11 4:45 AM;nzamosenchuk;Finally the root of the problem was spotted.

When performing actual indexing by placing the Document into the Directory, Lucene retrieves all data from the Field. Some fields contains TokenStream as a value. JCR uses own implementation named SingleTokenStream, for storing the value of _:PROPERTIES field. This class offers an Iterator pattern implementation by giving nextToken() method, but it holds just one value. And previously, when nextToken() invoked, the value is set to null, so the next invokation of nextToken() return null, finishing iteration process.
But, when Document is concurrently serialized by JBossCache Interceptor's thread and indexed in the VolatileIndex, reca conditions occurs. So sometime SingleTokenStream inside the Document is serialized with non-null value, but sometimes with null value. So coordinator receives Lucene Document with missing value of the field. 
Fix touched on serialization and iteraion in SingleTokemStream.

column1: Need to change WebDAV versioning mechanics to allow control checkin and checkout during PUT requests
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
For now versioning mechanism in WebDAV is defined by two parametes:
{{update-policy}} and {{auto-version}}

If the node is not versionable the only way to make it versionable is to set {{update-police=create-version}}. Though it would add appropriate mixin, it would also
do checkout-checkin. This behaviour can not be configured and that may cause some inconvenience (if, for example, we need not to make a new version after PUT, but will need to make one later).

Parameter {{auto-version}} allows to manage such situations, but it is considered only for {{update-policy=add}} and {{update-policy=replace}}. For add and replace update policies if node is not versionable we simply add or replace existing - we do not make it versionable and we can nothing do here.

The main idea is to make cases when we use {{update-policy=create-version}} to consider also {{auto-version}} parameter to be able make the node versionable from one side and manage checkin and checkout from another.
column277: 15/Sep/11 5:36 AM;nfilotto;In order to remain backward compatible, I propose to add a new value for {{update-policy}} like {{enable-versioning}}. In case we set {{update-policy}} to {{enable-versioning}}, it will automatically add the mixin {{mix:versionable}} to the node if needed and will "delegate" the checkin/checkout to the code that manages the parameter {{auto-version}}
column278: 15/Sep/11 7:38 AM;dkuleshov;According to WebDAV Versioning extension specification an unversioned resource can be put under version control with VERSION-CONTROL method. Our current webdav implementation supports this method. So if you need to make the node versionable you may use VERSION-CONTROL method. For versionable nodes you may use {{update-policy=replace}} and {{auto-version}} parameters to create new versions and manage checkin checkout operations.

column1: Allow to resynchronize the lucene indexes of each cluster node at start up
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
In JCR 1.14, it is possible to have dedicated indexes on each node of the cluster, however when a node leaves the cluster and goes back to it after a certain amount of time, if during this time window some write operations have been performed, the node will be de-synchronized with the rest of the cluster. The idea would be to add more conditions that will make the node re-index or get the indexes from the coordinator at start up, up to now it only occurs when the indexes are empty. It would be nice to have an open mechanism that allows us to add a set of conditions by configuration. We would need to implement a given interface and add the FQN of our implementation class to the list of filters in the config to add a new condition. If one of this filter returns true then the index recovery will be performed otherwise nothing will be done. By default we will always have the filter that check if the indexes are empty but we could provide 2 news filters:
# A filter that will simply check in the config if a given parameter (to define) is set to true
# A filter that will check if the total amount of docs is the same as the coordinator
column277:
14/Sep/11 3:31 PM;nzamosenchuk;Feature implemented and tested. When initializing a SearchIndex it checks if local index is really used and instantiates all the filters configured. This is made by checking if changes filter implements LocalIndexMarker interface.

Each filter in constructor performs required operations like RPC command's registration or whatever. Then calling stop on SearchManager invokes close() on each filter. This method should free the resources obtained by filter. When filters are initialized index invokes accept() on each one. When any returns true, current indexes dropped and reindexed or retrieved from coordinator node.

There are couple implementations of filters:
- DummyRecoveryFilter: always returns true, for cases when index must be recovered each time;
- SystemPropertyRecoveryFilter : return value of system property;
- DocNumberRecoveryFilter : checks number of documents in index on coordinator side and self-side. Return true is differs.

For more information please refer to JCR documentation. It is also updated with new feature paragraph (See QueryHandler configuration page).
column278: 15/Sep/11 4:49 AM;nfilotto;Sorry for the late remark but I did not notice that the filter uses a system property, actually I was expecting a filter based on a parameter of the query handler. So could you please add a new filter that does what I meant in the description of the filter #1. (No need to remove the filter based on the system property, it is already done so let's keep it)
column279:
16/Sep/11 3:30 AM;nzamosenchuk;New recovery filter added, documentation updated also.

- *org.exoplatform.services.jcr.impl.core.query.lucene.ConfigurationPropertyRecoveryFilter* : returns value of QueryHandler configuration property "index-recovery-filter-forcereindexing". So index recovery can be controlled from configuration separately for each workspace.

23/Sep/11 3:36 AM;nzamosenchuk;Documentation updated, an abstract is shown below.

h1. Asynchronous Re-indexing

Managing a big set of data using JCR in production environment sometimes requires special operations with Indexes, stored on File System. One of those maintenance operations is a recreation of it. Also called "re-indexing". There are various usecases when it's important to do. They include hardware faults, hard restarts, data-corruption, migrations and JCR updates that brings new features related to index. Usually index re-creation requested on server's startup or in runtime.

h2. On startup reindexing
Common usecase for updating and re-creating the index is to stop the server and manually remove indexes for workspaces requiring it. When server will be started, missing indexes are automatically recovered by re-indexing. JCR Supports direct RDBMS re-indexing, that usually is faster than ordinary and can be configured via QueryHandler parameter "rdbms-reindexing" set to "true" (for more information please refer to "Query-handler configuration overview").
New feature to introduce is asynchronous indexing on startup. Usually startup is blocked until process is finished. Block can take any period of time, depending on amount of data persisted in repositories. 
But this can be resolved by using an asynchronous approaches of startup indexation. Saying briefly, it performs all operations with index in background, without blocking the repository. This is controlled by the value of "async-reindexing" parameter in QueryHandler configuration.
With asynchronous indexation active, JCR starts with no active indexes present. Queries on JCR still can be executed without exceptions, but no results will be returned until index creation completed. Checking index state is possible via QueryManagerImpl:
{code:java}
((QueryManagerImpl)Workspace.getQueryManager()).getQueryHandeler().isOnline()
{code}

"OFFLINE" state means that index is currently re-creating. When state changed, corresponding log event is printed. From the start of background task index is switched to "OFFLINE", with following log event : "Setting index OFFLINE (repository/production[system])". When process finished, two events are logged : "Created initial index for 143018 nodes (repository/production[system])" and "Setting index ONLINE (repository/production[system])". Those two log lines indicates the end of process for workspace given in brackets. Calling isOnline() as mentioned above, will also return true.

h2. Hot Asynchronous Workspace Reindexing via JMX
Some hard system faults, error during upgrades, migration issues and some other factors may corrupt the index. Most likely end customers would like the production systems to fix index issues in run-time, without delays and restarts. Current versions of JCR supports "Hot Asynchronous Workspace Reindexing" feature. It allows end-user (Service Administrator) to launch the process in background without stopping or blocking whole application. Server can continue working as expected while index is recreated. This depends on the flag "allow queries", passed via JMX interface to reindex operation invocation. If the flag set, then application continues working. But there is one critical limitation the end-users must be aware. Index is frozen while background task is running. It meant that queries are performed on index present on the moment of task startup and data written into repository after startup won't be available through the search until process finished. Data added during re-indexation is also indexed, but will be available only when task is done. 
Briefly, JCR makes the snapshot of indexes on asynch task startup and uses it for searches. When operation finished, stale indexes replaced by newly created including newly added data. If flag "allow queries" is set to false, then all queries will throw an exception while task is running.
Current state can be acquired using the following JMX operation:
* getHotReindexingState - returns information about latest invocation: start time, if in progress or finish time if done.

h2. Notices
First of all, can't launch Hot re-indexing via JMX if index is already in offline mode. It means that index is currently is invoked in some operations, like re-indexing at startup, copying in cluster to another node  or whatever. Another important this is Hot Asynchronous Reindexing via JMX and "on startup" reindexing are completely different features. So you can't get the state of startup reindexing using command getHotReindexingState in JMX interface, but there are some common JMX operations:
* getIOMode - returns current index IO mode (READ_ONLY / READ_WRITE), belongs to clustered configuration states;
* getState - returns current state: ONLINE / OFFLINE.

    if [[ $fff -lt 50 ]] ; then

        echo -e "\n\nFile: $F"
        cat $F
        fi
    fi
    done

11/Aug/11 3:07 AM;areshetnyak;The node type nt:folder is not define default primary type for child nodes.
As result for this use case default primary type is null. 


In specification JSR-170 section 6.7.14 was described about DefaultPrimaryType :

{noformat}
getDefaultPrimaryType()

Gets the default node type that will be assigned to the
child node if it is created without an explicitly specified
node type. This node type must be a subclass of (or the
same class as) the node type(s) returned by
getRequiredPrimaryTypes.
If null is returned this indicates that no default primary
type is specified and that therefore an attempt to create
this node without specifying a node type will throw a
ConstraintViolationException. Note that to indicate a
null value for this attribute in a node type definition that
is stored in content, the jcr:defaultPrimaryType
property is simply removed (since null values for
properties are not allowed, see 6.7.20 Node Type
Definitions in Content).
{noformat}

So, for use case if default primary type not defined and no explicit primary type given to create a child node will throw a ConstraintViolationException.

column47:
Motivation:

For saving system resources we are stoping repositories what weren't used in some period of time (1 day or more). 
When the user come next time we launch repository again (this is a much shorter operation than restore from backup, because database and JCR index already exists)
But there's a possibility then user with existed (but stopped repository) will come just after start repository creation from backup and will be blocked by this process wich is take much  longer. So, we need to have possibility of multi threaded repository creation.

Detected changes to make repository creation multithreaded (proposed in patch):
# Remove synchronization from method RepositoryServiceImpl.createRepository().
# Make read and write operations in JDBCConfigurationPersister thread safe.
# Make using of RepositoryServiceConfiguration thread safe.

To reproduce the target env:

   1. Download PLF 3.0.3 from http://intranet.exoplatform.org/rest/jcr/repository/collaboration/Groups/platform/users/Documents/Releases/Platform/3.0.3/supported-binaries/platform
   2. Download the latest version of crash from here http://code.google.com/p/crsh/downloads/list
   3. add crash.war into tomcat/webapps
   4. add user.groovy into crash.war/WEB-INF/groovy/commands as described here https://github.com/exoplatform/gatein-stuff/tree/master/CRaSH
   5. connect to the JCR using crash then launch "user add -u foo -p password 10000" to create 10 thousands users

Once you have your 10 K users in PLF 3.0.3, restart your tomcat. At startup a query will be launched by ECMS that returns a lot of results and that takes a lot of time. The goal is to have a patch allowing to get the best performances in this context since it is the worse scenario for the ACL because:

   1. we have a lot of results
   2. we have a depth very big
   3. we have very few nodes with ACL set
   4. the cache size is very small (5000 entries)

25/Nov/11 3:14 AM;tolusha;The history of perf on the test RestoreOwnNodeTest was studied. 
The perf changing was checked from on revision 186 to current head for JCR 1.12.x and 1.14.x.

The perf on test RestoreOwnNodeTest is ~70 tps for 500 threads up to revision 3041 for JCR 1.12.x and 1.14.x.
After revision 3041 the perf was increased to ~120-160 tps for 500 threads  on JCR 1.12.x and 1.14.x.
The cause of increasing pref on this test on revision 3041 for JCR 1.12.x and 1.14.x is upgrading HDD subsystem tornado (RAID was upgraded).

The perf for this test on JCR 1.12.x  from revision 3041 to current head was not decreased.
The perf for this test on JCR 1.14.x  from revision 3041 to revision 4304 was not decreased, but on revision 4319 the perf is decrease from ~120-160 tps to ~90 tps on 500 threads.

The decrease perf in this test from rev. 4304 to rev. 4319 on JCR 1.14.x was tested locally on DB PostgreSLQ. As result this testing any regression from rev. 4304 to  rev.4319 on JCR1.14.x was not reproduced.

The perf for this test on JCR 1.14.x  from revision 4319 to revision 4615 was not decreased, but on revision 4632 the perf is decrease from  ~90 tps to ~67 tps on 500 threads.

According to https://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/TESTUKR-336 the caused code is changes in VoliteIndex at re.v 4632 But it is the same code as for 1.12.x

Need an issue on QA side to check perf for 1 threads to be able to profile test on Torando server.

05/Jan/12 2:43 AM;nzamosenchuk;Investigation on this issue lead to dead end. Some regression can be spotted on Postgre 8.4, but previous 8.3 version shows high performance of RestoreOwnNodeTest for both JCR 1.14 and 1.12. Next stage of research included re-runs of test on different versions and revisions. Problem that doesn't allow us to make concrete conclusions is stability of results. Revision 4304 showed regression comparing to previous, but same time, while relaunching it shows highest performance. But commit itself is nothing but POM modification in the cycle of JCR Release.
Next problem blocking us from finding out is profiling. First of all, JCR 1.12 and 14 has differences in data and command flows, but they can easily be spotted and handled. But profiling a 100 threaded test brings instability also. According to benchmark results launched under profiler, JCR 1.12 also faster, but profiler itself shows that 1.12 consumed more time than 1.14 have the same number of iteration. This picture has seen numerous times. Must admit that both JCRs shows high results when using outdated LinkedWorkspaceStorageCache. But nothing was found while researching things around JBoss Cache. Issue is currently considered to be closed since it consumed too much resources (around 20days and 4 developers worked on) with no results and no future ideas.

column47: Allow to use the system properties supported natively by lucene which are org.apache.lucene.FSDirectory.class to set the default FQN of the FSDirectory and org.apache.lucene.store.FSDirectoryLockFactoryClass to set the default FQN of the FSDirectoryLockFactory as we it is done in the patch for https://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR-1645. Maybe the easiest way would be to use FSDirectory.getDirectory instead of FSDirectory.open even if it is deprecated as it is done in the patch for JCR-1645. column277:
09/Aug/11 7:36 AM;nzamosenchuk;Done. Documentation updated. Here is an abstract:

By default JCR implementation uses optimal combination of Directory implementation and Lock Factory implementation. When running on OS different from Windows, NIOFSDirectory implementation used. And SimpleFSDirectory for Windows stations. NativeFSLockFactory is an optimal solution for wide variety of cases including clustered environment with NFS shared resources. But those default can be overridden with the help of system properties. There are two properties: "org.exoplatform.jcr.lucene.store.FSDirectoryLockFactoryClass" and "org.exoplatform.jcr.lucene.FSDirectory.class" that are responsible for changing default behavior. First one defines implementation of abstract Lucene LockFactory class and the second one sets implementation class for FSDirectory instances. For more information please refer to Lucene documentation. But be sure You know what You are changing. JCR allows end users to change implementation classes of Lucene internals, but doesn't guarantee it's stability and functionality.

column1: Lists stored into the cache can be inconsistent in cluster environment
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
In cluster env for example if:
# we have the list of all the children nodes of a given JCR node in the cluster node 1
# this list has not been loaded in the cluster node 2
# and we add a new child node in the cluster node 2

In this kind of usecase, since the list has not been loaded locally, we don't change the list content which has for consequences that the cluster node 1 doesn't have this new node in its list which is a consistency issue.

Please check this patch, then if it is ok apply it to the trunk, adapt it for JCR 1.12.x, create a JIRA and propose a patch for JCR 1.12.x. Since it is a critical bug it must be fixed asap in the branch JCR 1.12.x too.

column1: Reduce DB accesses to retrieve the ACL of a node
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
The ACL can be a performance killer when we have a big node depth and the ACL are very rarely set. In my use case, I used PLF 3.0.3 in which I created several thousands of users knowing that:
# for each user we create a page for the dashboard of the user 
# this dashboard is actually a node created by the MOP at depth of 12
# the ACL are very rarely created
# A JCR query is launched at startup by ECMS to upgrade the page of the MOP

Without the patch, tomcat starts in more than 1600 seconds with more than 166 000 queries
With the patch, tomcat starts in less than 700 seconds with more than 50 000 queries

The idea of the patch is:
# Limiting the scope of the ACL search, if we are only looking for the owner we stop the ACL search when we get the owner, if we are only looking for the permissions we stop the ACL search when we get the permissions
# Relying on Bloom filters in order to keep in memory all the ACL holders without consuming too much memory

As attached files please find the JProfiler results before and after the patch and the patch itself.

Please note that the patch is incomplete since the doc is missing and the parameters of the bloom filters should be configurable (aka falsePositiveProbability and expectedNumberOfElements) moreover we should allow to disable the bloom filters by configuration

05/Aug/11 4:32 AM;pnedonosko;This _old perf killer_ and _ugly lock_ is needed to prevent {{FileNotFoundException}} exceptions in the JCR values storage during concurrent read-write of Values (add and delete). On some file-systems, like _extfs_ on *nixes, an application will not see the removal of a file until it will not try to read from it again (i.e. doesn't lock by read operation). But on an another, like _Microsoft NTFS_, file/folder cannot be deleted while opened by an another application. 
This issue shows that this mechanism was omitted (by mistake I guess) in JCR 1.14 codebase and now you had returned it back to the state how it works in JCR 1.12. But it also shows that we can get better performance without in-row locking (what Semaphore does there).

@Nicolas you're code owner now and I, as Platform productization and QA side, ask you to provide both, performance and consistency, in the JCR 1.14. 
It's recommended to do not _remove it completely from the code as long as we don't have good proof that it is required_. It might introduce real problems for real customers. You can issue work on fragment-based locks to implement _smarter mechanism_ and prove the problem and solution by new tests, QA will be glad to run them.

column1: Improve Permission management in case of a JCR Query
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Up to now except when we set explicitly a limit, all the ScoreNode are checked to see if we have access to it which can be dramatic in term of performances when we have a huge result set.

This patch does the following things:
# In case of a search with an explicit order clause, the permissions are lazy-loaded such that if we want the x first nodes only the needed nodes will be loaded
# In case of a search with no explicit order clause, we had a threshold (in the patch it is hard coded to 100 but it should be configurable) if the result set doesn't contain more elements than the threshold, the current behavior is kept (i.e. all nodes are loaded to be sorted by path) otherwise the nodes are not sorted to prevent affecting too much the performances
# In case of a system session, the access permissions are not checked

column47:
When browser performs {{GET}} request for non-latin named collection WebDAV response is malformed. For example, if we have a collection(folder) named "{{@}}" located at {{http://host:port/rest/jcr/repository/production/}} and we're performing {{GET}} request (via browser) for {{http://host:port/rest/jcr/repository/production/@}} we receive something like {code}..{code} because collection "{{@}}" is empty. The address bar will be {{http://host:port/rest/jcr/repository/production/%40}} And if we press "{{..}}" to go one level up (obviously to {{http://host:port/rest/jcr/repository/production}}) we receive blank page and the address bar is {{http://172.19.20.24:8080/rest/jcr/repository/production/%4}} If we glance to the source code of the page we see {code:xml}
..
{code} The href element is incorrect, it should be {code:xml} .. {code} The origin of this bug is located within {{exo.jcr.component.webdav/src/main/resources/xslt/get-method.xsl}} file. (After XSLT it is used in GET response body) If you check the file lines you can see {code:xml}
..
{code} The mistake is that {{sv:name}} is not URL encoded and in our case equals "{{@}}" so it's length is 1 and {{xlink:href}} is URL encoded so we have "{{%40}}" instead of "{{@}}" and its length is 3, so value of href element {code:xml}{code} finally equals {code:xml}http://172.19.20.24:8080/rest/jcr/repository/production/%4{code}
