column1: Multi DB Schema Support
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Basically, Oracle can have more then one schema inside it.

exo-jcr doesn't manage this case and if we try to connect differents exo-instance with different schema under the same DB
we will get this e oracle error   "ORA-00942: table or view does not exist"

this problem will returned when the table or view exists but is in a different schema from the current schema where the SQL is executing
(in other word, the table doesn't own by the user1, but owned by other another user user2), the oracle ORA-00942 error will returned.


This problem can be Resolved by explicitly reference the table or view by specifying the schema name, i.e. schema_name.table_name.

column279:
23/Jun/11 7:57 AM;sergiykarpenko;Thanks to Anatoly, I understand why performance depends from getChildNodesData in ChildAxisQuery

Lets check our usecase

We want find node by path
 "/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt/jcr:content"
with query
  "select * from nt:base where dc:title = 'Exoplatform' and jcr:path like '/teststorage/root2/%'"

1) How it works with getChildNodesData
 * ChildAxisQuery$SimpleChildrenCalculator.getHits()  takes root-node child nodes with getChildNodesData(). Result is "teststorage", and this node is cached.
  IMPORTANT: getChildNodesData assigned parent-nodes ACL to child nodes. Thats why "teststorage" cached WITH ACL.
 * ChildAxisQuery$SimpleChildrenCalculator.getHits()  takes child nodes for "teststorage". Same algoritm and comments. "root2" with ACL is cached.

 * query does some job. Thats not impotant.
 * on 
    - QueryResultImpl.getResuls(QueryResultImpl.java:329)
    - QueryResultImpl.isAccessGranted(QueryResultImpl.java:413)
 takes all result nodes 
    - VersionableWorkspaceDataManager.getItemData is called 

 * VersionableWorkspaceDataManager.getItemData takes a node and ACLInheritanceSupportedWorkspaceDataManager.getNearestACAncestorAcl(node) is called.
 * ACLInheritanceSupportedWorkspaceDataManager.getNearestACAncestorAcl(node) traverse all nodes from the end, until any node with acl is fetched.

So, for node /teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt/jcr:content there is next calls:
  
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt/jcr:content
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9
/teststorage/root2/node2
/teststorage/root2 - and this is finish, because root2 is cached and contains ACL.


2) How it works without getChildNodesData

 Same steps.
 With single exception - "teststorage" and "root2" cached WITHOUT ACL.

For node /teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt/jcr:content there is next calls:
  
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt/jcr:content
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5
/teststorage/root2/node2/node9
/teststorage/root2/node2
/teststorage/root2
/teststorage
/                - yep, root node always have ACL

There is two extended getItemData calls. And moreover, when "teststorage" and "root2" became fetched and cached, thay will be cached WITHOUT ACL. 
Thats why, redundant calls will be repeated all times.


Why preformance in our usecase was so dramaticaly decreased?

Because, search result contain 10 nodes on same level (/teststorage/root2/node2/node9/node5/1-9-5-2.txt/jcr:content - 7 nodes). 
For each node - 2 redundant getItemData calls on QueryResultImpl.getResuls() and fetching result with NodeIterator. So there is 40 redundatn calls per single usecase run.

column1: Avoid data accesses in case of new created nodes
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47: Up to now, we don't check if the node is new before collecting data from the data access layer for example if the node is new it makes no sense to get its children from the data access layer since we already know that he doesn't have any persisted children. The idea of the provided patch is to avoid the best we can to call the DB when it is useless.

column1: Different behavior between Mysql and HSQL when creating contents with same name and different cases
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
When testing I've found a different behavior between Mysql DB and HSQL DB.
under a node where same name sibling is disabled,using HSQL, I can add nodes with same names but with different cases like "Test" and "TEST". this is not possible using Mysql.
I've attached an XML export [^same-name-category.xml] containing two nodes with the same name created under HSQLDB which can not be imported using MySQL .

column277: 13/May/11 10:25 AM;nfilotto;Case sensitivity is explained here http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.1/en/case-sensitivity.html, we could for example set the charset name and the collation name directly at table creation using variables in the SQL script that can be set thanks to the configuration, using by default the most common charset name and the most common case sensitive collation name
column278: 22/Jul/11 4:20 AM;tolusha;It is administrative task. If admin decided to create database with special charset and collation we then override it and cause unexpected behavior.
column279:
22/Jul/11 5:09 AM;ali_hamdi;Technically, I agree that this is a technical aspect that customer should decide.
But functionally, here we are in front of a strange behavior of JCR, sometimes it accepts names with same names and different cases and sometimes it is not. We should provide a unique behavior for JCR or at least make sure that this is indicated on documentation.

column1: Allow to create sessions from ACLs
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
I explain the need first. In authenticated mode, there's a request to cache contents and share the cache for all users. We need to retrieve the contents first then we use a portlet cache to cache the resulting markup and share it between users.

We have three ways to retrieve contents from the JCR :
- System : if we use this, we will end up with contents visible by unauthorized users
- User session : if we use this, the first to access the contents will cache the results. Thus, the resulting markup is based on the first user to access them. The resulting effect is like the System session, we end up with possible visible contents, not authorized for some users.
- Anonymous : The last one, if we're authenticated, we can still create an anonymous session. But, we will then see the "public" contents only (with "Any READ" permission). For an intranet need, it's not enough. Most of the time, a folder will contain public contents ("Any READ") and intranet contents ("*:/platform/users READ"). Thus, when authenticated, you see more contents than in public mode.


So, the request is to be able for WCM Services to create a fake session (like we do with the anonymous one)
Here is a proposal of a possible call :
SessionProvider.createProvider(List<AccessControlEntry> accessList);
accessList==null or empty : anonymous session
ACL = {"*:/platform/users READ"} => we have a private session

This is just an example to demonstrate our final need.

column1: Allow to reindex a repository/workspace thanks to JMX
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
The idea of this task is to be able to re-index a repository or a workspace thanks to JMX without having to manually stop the server then remove the index directory then restart the server. This is mainly useful for Administrators that would like to re-index without making the whole platform available. It can also be interesting for cluster nodes that have been stopped during a certain period of time when we enable the mode where all the cluster nodes have their own, their indexes are outdated to we would like to silently refresh them.

So we will expose through JMX, 2 methods which are:
* indexRepository(String repositoryName, boolean dropExistingIndexes)
* indexWorkspace(String repositoryName, String workspaceName, boolean dropExistingIndexes)

* When the parameter dropExistingIndexes == true, we fully reindex the repository/workspace by dropping first the index repository then reindex the content. The expected behavior is exactly the behavior of the application when we drop the directory and restart the JCR, expect that the indexing will be blocking which means that an exception will be thrown anytime we will try to execute a query. Please note that in case, we are in a cluster environment and we configured the mode where only the coordinator manages the indexes, it would mean that all the nodes will have to be aware that an indexing is in progress and thus should throw an exception anytime we will try to execute a query like we were trying to index the node locally. Moreover if we call the JMX method on a non coordinator node, it must delegate it to the coordinator. In case all the nodes have their own indexes, if we call the JMX method on node, it will re-index only on the local node.

* When the parameter dropExistingIndexes == false, we fully reindex the repository/workspace without dropping the previous index which means that we will sill be able to execute queries on the node (no exception will be thrown), the re-indexing will be done silently. The side effect is that removed nodes could still be available in the indexes.

column1: Consider to use Trove collections
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
The goal of this task is to identify all the places in the code from kernel to jcr where we have a primitive collections (not sorted as it is not supported so LinkedHashMap, LinkedHashSet, TreeMap or TreeSet must be ignored) and replace them with the corresponding Trove Collections as it is supposed to be faster and less memory consuming than the java.util collections.

See below all the places that I have identified in the code:

*jcr.core*

* DBRestrore -> columnType -> List<Integer>
* ChildAxisQuery$ChildAxisScorer -> docIds -> List<Integer>
* ChildAxisQuery$SimpleChildrenCalculator -> uuids -> Map<Integer, String>
* ParentAxisQuery$ParentAxisScorer -> scores -> Map<Integer, Float>
* QueryConstants -> OPERATION_NAMES -> Map<Integer, String>
* QueryConstants -> TYPE_NAMES -> Map<Integer, String>
* SysViewWorkspaceInitializer$SVNodeData -> childNodesMap -> HashMap<InternalQName, Integer>
* JDBCWorkspaceDataContainer.getDataRestorer(DataRestoreContext context) -> convertColumnIndex -> Set<Integer>
* QueryHitsQuery$QueryHitsQueryScorer -> scores -> Map<Integer, Float>
* CachingMultiIndexReader -> readersByCreationTick -> Map<Long, OffsetReader>
* Recovery -> losers -> Set<Long>
* Recovery.run() -> transactionIds -> Set<Long>

*jcr.ext*

* BackupChainLog.getJobEntryStates() -> infos -> HashMap<Integer, JobEntryInfo>

*jcr.webdav*

* WebDavConst -> statusDescriptions -> Hashtable<Integer, String>

*kernel.container*

* ManagedMethodMetaData -> parameters -> Map<Integer, ManagedMethodParameterMetaData>

*ws.commons*

* URI -> defaultPorts -> Hashtable<String, Integer>

*ws.rest.core*

* UriTemplateParser -> groupIndexes -> List<Integer>
column277: 29/Mar/11 12:39 PM;nfilotto;Please note that apart a Set and a Map, trove proposes collections that are not compatible with the interfaces of java.util which means that at first glance the CollectionFactory will be limited to Map and Set. If we want to really benefit from trove, I believe that we have to tie our code to trove, so the question is does-it still make sense to use trove?

column285:
11/May/12 7:18 AM;dkuleshov;Not sure if collections are used a lot during daily testing, but I can try to explain the performance and memory consumption results. 
{quote}The standard HashMap holds a Map.Entry object for each of its 
elements. Trove uses open addressing, and hence gets around this 
problem with chaining. You can still use Map.entrySet on a Trove Map, 
but it is a Bad Thing. This will cause Trove to create the Map.Entry 
objects that it tries to get away from, so if possible, don't use these 
operations. If you buy into Trove, you can go down a path that couples 
you tightly to the Trove collections. You can implement Trove specific 
APIs (forEachEntry, forEachKey, forEachValue, and transformValues) to 
potentially gain higher performance.  {quote} ([Source link|http://onjava.com/pub/a/onjava/2002/06/12/trove.html])

In other words to benefit from trove collections we must avoid to use 
{{Map.Entry}} and {{Map.entrySet()}}. And if I look in, for example, kernel 
sources, I find about 60 places where {{Map.Entry}} is used and about 
50 places where {{Map.entrySet()}}. This impacts not only performance, 
but it also impacts memory consumption, because it forces trove 
collections to create extra entities besides its original.

I assume we'll have to rewrite huge part of our source code to get real benefit of this library.
column286: 11/May/12 7:49 AM;nfilotto;Thanks for clarifications to avoid having to re-write everything could you please keep sun collections in all places where we use {{Map.Entry}} and {{Map.entrySet()}} and use Trove collections only where we don't use them. And of course check if it is used during the daily tests. Once done, I guess we can retry to test it in term of perfs and memory consumption.
column287:
15/May/12 4:50 AM;dkuleshov;Recently I profiled on my developers machine and made some other tests and the results were quite unexpected. Sun collections lib, as you can see here: [^Call_Tree_Sun.html], takes in average ~3.1% of total benchmark execution time. Trove collections lib ([^Call_Tree_Trove.html]) takes in average ~1.5%. This obviously means that trove collections should be twice faster. But in general it is only ~1% performance boost (not considering estimation errors caused by environment), so benchmark test may not indicate this, because usually it deviates more.
Another interesting thing is that the most time-consuming operation in trove collection is {{gnu.trove.map.hash.THashMap.<init>()}} (~1%), not {{gnu.trove.map.hash.THashMap.entrySet}} (~0%), so previous assumption seems to be irrelevant. Thus I guess there is nothing we can improve here.

* Backup doesn't work itself due to JNDI problem (WCM Cloud adopters faced same problem)
* JCR Search isn't workable during the backup time, what broke concept introduced in JCR Backup feature in previous versions fo JCR. Backup has to be transparent and should not crash other processes (you may stop all incomers in a latch lock for example).

column1: JCR configuration update require dropping JCR_CONFIG table
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
After changing JCR configuration file, portal/WEB-INF/conf/jcr/repository-configuration.xml, updating session-max-age value, I see no change after restart.
It appears JCR store its configuration on JCR_CONFIG table and this table should be dropped to see new configuration taken in account.

It's critical for ADM/IT team :

* They could be in situation where it's just forbidden to do such operation.
* JCR configuration may be tuned differently by instances, it's incompatible with this approach (centric vision)

JCR should honor xml configuration files whatever exist in JCR_CONFIG table.

column47:
REST methods what contain repository as parameter should be removed because:
1. This method can internally change current repository name. It can be a way to access one repository from other. Example:
tenant1.localhost:8080/rest/registry/tenant2/......

acces from repository "tenant1" to repository "tenant2"

2. This method blocking access to cloud-aware method RESTRegistryService.getEntry(String)
Example:
Request tenant1.localhost:8080/rest/registry/exo:application/...... 
will be intercepted by RESTRegistryService.getEntry(String, String) method
and RESTRegistryService.getEntry(String) will never be called

column1: IndexInfos.write() should be called just after replaceIndexes operation done by IndexMerger
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
IndexInfos are used to store (and replicate) the list of actual current Lucene Directories in JCR index. When merge is done this list should be written (both replicated if talking in terms of clustered env.) asap, for other cluster nodes to be aware of it.
This issue should be checked if IndexInfos.write() are indeed not invoked after merge is done. This operation is only done by MultiIndex.flush() now, but flush is not invoked in merging cycle. 

So on coordinator we'll see the following:
1) merging and updating the list of indexes in-memory, so indexes marked for deletion will no longer be used by new MultiReaders
2) When the flush will be invoked later (by executer or b some later save()), indexInfow will be written and obsolete indexes will  deleted.
So on coordinator node obsolete indexes will be deleted "some time" after update of index list.

But non-coordinator cluster nodes will be notified of new indexes and right after the will be deleted by coordinator (see flush() code).

column277:
02/Feb/11 10:07 AM;nzamosenchuk;Successfully upgraded to lucene 2.9.

What was changed/done:
1. Query class: changed definition (visibility modifier) of createWeight(..) method.
2. Interface Weight replaced with it's abstract type.
3. Weight.score(IndexReader) replaced with Weight.score(IndexReader, boolean, boolean). 
4. IndexReader.getSequenceReaders() introduced and used in Lucene internals for per-segment search and caching. In our custom IndexReader should be overridden and return null (This is safe solution and confirmed within lucene's mailing list by Simon Willnauer).
5. FSdirectory.getDirectory(...) replaced with FSdirectory.open(...). But open(...) doesn't create a directory structure anymore.
6. Term can be null, when reader.termDocs(Term) invoked. Adding safe check to avoid NPE. 
7. Got rid of HitCollector in favor of Collector class.

column1: Reduce the total amount of queries needed to update a property
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
During my perf tests, I realized that we launch several queries that could be avoided for example we always try to remove the references, we also drop all the values and re-add the new ones. In this patch proposal, I tried a new logic that get the previous property type in order to know if it is needed to remove the references and I evaluate the total amount of previous values in order to know which values need to be deleted (if needed), which values need to be updated and which values need to be added.

I launch on my local machine the daily perf tests with 100 iterations, and it seems that the perfs are about the same on nearly all tested db (i.e. HSQLDB, MySQL MyISAM, MySQL InnoDB and PostgreSQL) and much better on Oracle (avg response time without the patch is 3,68 ms and with the patch 2,66 ms). Those results have to be validated by the QA, if we have same or better performances with less queries, I think it makes sense to apply the patch because I believe that the less we have queries so more scalable our JCR will be.

As attached files, you will find the patch to validate and to clean (javadoc is missing, need to check if everything is closed properly...) and all the statistics

column1: Propose a re-indexing mechanism for RDBMS
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
All our customers configure the JCR to use a RDBMS with or without a FS for the Value Storage, so the idea would be to propose a special procedure for them that will be much faster than what we currently propose that needs to visit all the nodes of all the workspace which will be very slow in case of a big workspace. It is critical for our customers to propose reliable and fast way to re-index a workspace. So we need to implement a special way to re-index a workspace for RSBMS. 

The Idea would be to launch a complex query to get all the nodes and their properties of a given workspace at the same time (like FIND_NODES_BY_PARENTID_CQ_QUERY but for all the nodes of the workspace and all their properties). A good way to parse the result, would be to load all the properties in a special NodeData type in order to avoid getting any property from the database and offer the Node to an Indexing Queue (a BlockingQueue) that will be processed concurrently by a pool of threads. Once all the nodes have been indexed, the thread pool will be destroyed.

* The old manner took 32 m to index 70 000 nodes which means an average of 27 s to index 1 000 nodes
* The new manner without using the ID approach used for MySQL and PosgreSQL (i.e. what we currently have into svn), took 15 m to index 71 000 nodes which means an average of 12 s to index 1 000 nodes. I noticed that the page size did not seem to have any impact on the perf.
* The new manner with the ID approach used for MySQL and PosgreSQL, took 18 m to index 71 000 nodes which means an average of 15 s to index 1 000 nodes.

The methods Node.getProperties(String namePattern)/Node.getNodes(String namePattern) can be interesting when we have a lot of properties/nodes to get and we would like to avoid executing several SQL queries instead of one (assuming that the cache doesn't contain any of those properties/nodes). Up to now, we get all the properties/nodes and we filter them programmatically, unfortunately this approach reduces the total amount of use cases where this method is useful, for example when a Node has a lot of properties/nodes and we want to get few properties/nodes it could be faster to get property/node by property/node instead of using this method.
The idea would be to convert the pattern into a SQL filter to add to our SQL query and get all expected properties/nodes in one single query.

As we all know, the current solution is not acceptable for PLF and EPPSP, since it is not really scalable and the data is available for all nodes only after a certain amount of time, so we have to allow:

0. Each node to have its volatile index in order to have near real time results on each nodes not only on the coordinator as it is now
1. Each node to have its own indexes in order to scale more in read and write and to avoid issues related to the shared file systems
2. Since #1 can be an issue when we want to add dynamically a new node to the cluster because the node won't have its own indexes, we need to be able to get the indexes from the coordinator.

06/Dec/10 2:30 AM;nzamosenchuk;There are few issues related to sending query as string:
1. additional cost for coordinator to parse the query. It is rather resource consuming (including javaCC parser and other elements of query-dataflow).
2. There will be double node-retrieval. Once query executed we'll have to retrieve all results. If division on client | coordinator layers  is made on topper level as proposed, the result of the queries on that level is nodes (NodeImpls). So we'll have to retrieve the node's from queryResult, read their UUIDs, send the list of UUIDs to client, retrieve NodeImpls from SessionDataManager by UUID.
3. This will require a SessionImpl present in QueryHandler from the beginning of lifecycle (see above). So additional hack for Session injection required.

23/Dec/10 9:45 AM;nfilotto;To clarify the work the we did and we still need to do:
What we did:
1. We try to execute the queries on the coordinator but it was a failure so we abort this study, so the related changes can even be reverted if.
2. We try to replicate Lucene Document instead of ids, the results are not as good as expected but at least they are better than what we currently have so we keep them

The next steps are:
3. Instead of having one single volatile index in the coordinator, we will allow to have a volatile index in all the cluster nodes (even if it can cause consistency issues) but only the coordinator will be able to flush the volatile index into the disc. This way the other nodes will be aware of the latest changes sooner. When the coordinator flushes the volatile index, all the volatile indexes must be cleared

4. We will propose another search filter that will allow to have lucene indexes per cluster node, this approach is in fact 2 + 3 + the fact that all nodes will be able to flush their volatile indexes independently (like in JCR 1.10.x). The indexes will be local so we should be more scalable

11/Mar/11 5:42 AM;nzamosenchuk;Local Index has been passed through brief performance testing in clustered environment. It was compared to default implementation, when shared index was used without any volatile indexes on non=coordinator nodes. Testing was performed in a cluster made of developer's PCs (class of Intel Core2Quad 2.8 Ghz) with separated Mod_JK balancer, NFS server and Oracle 11g. Network is 100 Mbit Ethernet.
Two types of tests used:
a) WebdavAddPFTest : performs PDF file uploading with defined mimetype. PDF size is 60 KB (write test).
b) WebdavQueryTest : performs JCR-query execution via WebDav (query test).

Each test was executed for few time in 48 threads, with 20 and 100 iterations accordingly for write and query test in a cluster from 1 to 3 nodes.
The results of the testing are as following.

For default coordinator-oriented implementation with shared index:
test  | 1 | 2 | 3 | <- cluster size
Write: |6.85 | 7.00 | 5.45 |
Query: | 870 | 1384 | 1883 |


For local index implementation:
test  | 1 | 2 | 3 | <- cluster size
Write: |7.13 | 7.61 | 7.77 |
Query: | 959 | 1708 | 2099 |

Summing up must admit, Local Index implementation shows results not worse than default implementation for both query and write usecases. It even offers better results in term of scalability. Take in account greatly reduced latency of search result availability in clustered environment.

column1: User profiles initialization listeners are not triggered for LDAP users (LDAP Users can not access to any File Explorer drive)
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Summary : when a LDAP user tries to access to any drives in file explorer portlet, he gets a PathNotFoundException.

Description:
When you create a user by eXo User interface, there is an event that is triggered and will invoke a listener named "dms.new.user.event.listener"(see organization-component-plugins-configuration.xml) to initialize newly created user profile (adding him to the default group (/platform/users) , defining the user HOMEPATH and creating his personnel drives).

Unfortunately, this listener is triggered only when creating a user by eXo. 
In fact, if you add a user with an interface outside eXo (DB interface, LDAP Interface, AD Interface or any other application), this listener won't be triggered.

Thus, new user profile is not properly initialized.

Steps to Reproduce :
1)Install Open LDAP server and include necessary schema in $OpenLDAPInstallHome\slapd.conf (see attached slapd.conf)
2)Follow the OpenLDAP secion in: http://community.jboss.org/wiki/GateInwithLDAPinreadonlymode and do not use their attached file picketlink-idm-openldap-acme-config.xml, just use the one attached to this issue.
3)Connect to wcm as root/gtn, navigate to users and groups management portlet and
add "jduke" user (for example) to required groups to access to Site Explorer portlet(/platform/users, /platform/administrators,..)
4)Logout and Login as jduke/theduke and navigate to site explorer
5)Click on the "private" or the "public" drives you will get the error message : Path not found!Maybe, It was removed or path changed! (see attached PathNotFoundException.JPG)
Moreover,click on any other drive you will get a PathNotFoundException Exception (see attached exception.log).

It seems like listeners involved in the initialization of user profiles are not triggered for LDAP users

There is study: http://wiki-int.exoplatform.org/display/exoproducts/Indexing+managed+by+chunks

Implement the chunk approach with JBC in a dedicated branch, and compare the results of http://tests.exoplatform.org/JCR/1.14.0-CR1/rev.3100/japex-reports/AddNtFileWithMetadataTestCleanDBOracle/oracle/1/1.1/index.html in a cluster or a non cluster environment with what we currently have
column50:
Planning required works, reviewing the code, thinking over architecture changes.
Reviewing MultiIndex/SingleIndex code related to Hierarchy resolution over Lucene directory, came to conclusion, that current impl should be based on MultiIndex.
Sometimes (i.e. Path-oriented queries) searcher must know hierarchy relations between JCR content nodes, that are indexed in to the directory as lucene documents. To speed up search in those cases, current implementation store those relations directly in the lucene documents, so it can be retrieved without accessing the DB or any outer layers (cache or etc). This is possible thanks to DocId - the document identifier inside directory. But this is unique only within directory. When talking about SingleIndex - DocId is fully enough to build up JCR node relations. But when there are multiple indexes, there must an information containing the index handle and doc identifier in it. MultiIndex uses offsets for those purposes. So the mechanism of hierarchy resolution becomes much more complicated.
So chunk approach is more like modification of MultiIndex, with limitations, rather then SingleIndex with additions.;07/Oct/10 2:51 AM;nzamosenchuk;28800

column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Working on this issue ( http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR-1438 ) was found that on restore node the versionable child is deleting.

Two potential solution of this problem was found :
1) Adding vesionable child tree in ChangesLog of restore.
2) In ChengesLog of restore not remove versioned child node.

1st solution is more rapid in the implementation, but may reduce the restore performance, in case the versioned child node has a large tree with heavy content.

2nd solution is more complicated to implementation, but should not reduce the restore performance (because vesiobale child should not be delete on restore).

As part of this issue ( http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR-1438 ) was implemented 1st solution to solve problem with deleting vesionable child on restore.

In this issue will be implemented 2nd solution.

column1: LuceneQueryBuilder have incomplete PropertyTypeRegistry
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Debugging testcase attached to https://jira.jboss.org/browse/EXOJCR-924 shows that PropertyTypeRegistry is not completely filled.

The reason is:
- On NodeTypeDataManagerImpl.start() nodetypes are extracted from "nodetypes.xml"
- than PropertyTypeRegistry created using NodeTypeDataManagerImpl
- all properties registered in NodeTypeDataManagerImpl are copied to PropertyTypeRegistry, so PropertyTypeRegistry contains property only from "nodetypes.xml";
- after that RepositoryServiceImpl.registerNodeTypes(String repositoryName) registers all test nodetypes to NodeTypeDataManagerImpl.

So NodeTypeDataManagerImpl will contain full list of properties, but PropertyTypeRegistry will contain only from "nodetypes.xml".

After test restart ( and same database) new NodeTypeDataManagerImpl will be filled from database, and all property types will be placed to PropertyTypeRegistry.

This bug was not detected before because LuceneQueryBuilder.getStringValues() can handle unknown propeties.

column1: Allow to exclude nodes from query results
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
The goal of this task would be to give the ability to disable the indexing on nodes that are sub nodes of excluded paths and/or that are of a given type using new "indexing rules" (which means that we could have several excluded paths and node types). See below a potential example:
{code}
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE configuration SYSTEM "http://www.exoplatform.org/dtd/indexing-configuration-1.3.dtd">
<configuration xmlns:exo="http://www.exoplatform.com/jcr/exo/1.0">
  <exclude nodeType="exo:hiddenable"/>
  <exclude path="/my[2]/path"/>
  <exclude nodeType="exo:foo" path="/my/other[2]/path"/>
</configuration>
{code}

In the example above, the indexing will be disabled:
* for all nodes of type {{exo:hiddenable}} in the whole workspace
* for the node corresponding to the path {{/my[2]/path}} and all its descendants
* for all the nodes under the path {{/my/other[2]/path}} of type {{exo:foo}}

17/Aug/10 4:34 AM;tolusha;As I understand from usecase you need to make copy of node with its version history inside one repository. It just not supported by VersionHistoryImporter.

After importing node with UUID behavior IMPORT_UUID_CREATE_NEW you just create new node with new version history and you can't not do importing version history of old node into new one. That is why you got an exception.

That your usecase would work you have 2 choice:
1. Use UUID behavior IMPORT_UUID_COLLISION_REMOVE_EXISTING instead of IMPORT_UUID_CREATE_NEW
2. Remove old node before importing

As I understand the allowable size of the field CONFIG enough that would write a complete configuration of the JCR.
After tenant creation the full JCR configuration is stored in the table JCR_CONFIG and eventually field size 65KB can be insufficiently.

For MySQL 
BLOB = L + 2 bytes (max size is 2^16 - 1 or 65,535 bytes, 65KB)
MEDIUMBLOB = L + 3 bytes (max size is 2^24 - 1 or 16,777,215 bytes, 16MB)
LONGBLOB = L + 4 bytes (max size is 2^32 - 1 or 4,294,967,295 bytes, 4GB)

1. We propose to increase the type of field CONFIG to LONGBLOB for MySql
2. Check other databases on the possibility to write to the field "CONFIG in the table" JCR_CONFIG  the data with size of about 100 Mb

column1: Use cached table for HSLQLDB tables
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Default configuration for tables created in HSQLDB keeps all the data in memory (even if it is persistent). It would make sense memory wise to improve that and create "cached" tables that keep only a part of the data in memory and not everything.

It is a cheap and easy way to lower the memory used by GateIn and the components above. While this won't have any impact on the production systems, it will have an impact on GateIn developers that use hsqldb by default.

So instead of using "create table" to create hsqldb tables, using "create cached table" will take care of that. For reference here are some excerpt of hsqldb manual:

A good plus would be to make this easily configurable somehow.

"The three types of persistent tables are MEMORY tables, CACHED tables and TEXT tables.

Memory tables are the default type when the CREATE TABLE command is used. Their data is held entirely in memory but any change to their structure or contents is written to the <dbname>.script file. The script file is read the next time the database is opened, and the MEMORY tables are recreated with all their contents. So unlike TEMP table, the default, MEMORY tables are persistent.

CACHED tables are created with the CREATE CACHED TABLE command. Only part of their data or indexes is held in memory, allowing large tables that would otherwise take up to several hundred megabytes of memory. Another advantage of cached tables is that the database engine takes less time to start up when a cached table is used for large amounts of data. The disadvantage of cached tables is a reduction in speed. Do not use cached tables if your data set is relatively small. In an application with some small tables and some large ones, it is better to use the default, MEMORY mode for the small tables."

Our goal is to integrate Tika into eXo JCR and for this we have 2 ways which are the following:
1. Get rid of the DocumentReaderService and replace it with Tika
2. Create a DocumentReader based on Apache Tika

To be able to choose between those 2 solutions, we must first study the extensibility of Tika in order to ensure that we can easily do what we can do with the current implementation which are:
* If for some reason one parser doesn't work as we expect, we can easily replace it. 
* If I have a special document type, I can create my own parser 

If those 2 features are possible with Tika and can be done as easily as with the DocumentReaderService, then we will implement #1 otherwise we will implement #2

To be able to judge if it is easy or not to do those 2 features, I expect as result of this task a Tutorial for both of those features.

column1: JCR path management improvement
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Original source: http://wiki-int.exoplatform.org/display/exoproducts/JCR+path+management+study

I have invested a considerable amount of resources doing benchmarking of JCR with GateIn as use case in mind. I am also quite familliar with a part of the JCR source code that I have investigated (the path management part). This study is based on my experience in optimization and driven by GateIn use cases. This page is about facts and critics (critics is my personal opinion and is honnestly fair, specially when it comes to performances) and it focuses on a single aspect of the JCR runtime which is how path are used in the engine.

Tests results and kernel + jcr patches are attached to the pages.

Assumptions:
My optimization are mainly based on two facts

* Object immutability is usually good
*Usage of the String#intern() method leading to better performance is a myth

Context:
* Tests have been executed on a core i7 machine with 8 gigs of RAM
* GateIn 3.0 trunk is used (close to GA) with JCR 1.12.0-CR2
* JProfiler 6 is used for doing performance investigation
* JMeter is used as injector
* JVM is tuned with "-Xms512m -Xmx1024m -XX:MaxPermSize=256m" setting to avoid memory to be a bottleneck
* JCR eviction policy is changed to org.jboss.cache.eviction.ExpirationAlgorithm instead of FIFO (FIFO creates much contention, around 20%)

Tests (facts):
3 tests comparing 2 different versions of GateIn are performed, the GateIn versions

* intern() : actually the CR2 release untouched
* immutable : the CR2 release with String.intern() removed and the design of a few objects have changed (mainly the path objects) to be immutable

Test 1: object creation
Object creation is tested with the display of 2000 GateIn pages by a single user. JProfiler is configured to track the whole org.exoplatform.services.jcr package and the number of objects created in that package.

* intern:  60,000,000 objects were created during the test
* immutable: 50,000,000 objects were allocated during the test

Test 2 - Hotspot
The hotspot tests displays the hotspot inside JCR package. The test is performed with 4000 page displays done by 4 threads with no think time. It is not possible to go above 4 threads as, the JVM instrumentation for the profiling does not allow it. The goal of this test is to compare the inherent time spent in the JCR layer. The test shows two things:

* the immutable version is more efficient with less inherent time
* the time spent in the path management changes: the creation of path costs less, however comparing InternalQName increases which is normal as it is a tradeoff done by the removal of String#intern() removal. Under load the String#intern() is a serious bottleneck (not demonstrated here but can be shown easily).

Test 3 - Global throughput
The last test does not use jprofiler and use only jmeter to show the difference of throughput between the two versions. The test is performed by 32 threads showing 2 pages with no think time (which means it is quite aggressive). The number of pages shown is the same as each thread will perform 500 iterations. The result shows that the throuhgput with the immutable version is better:

* intern(): 74 requests/second
* immutable: 87 requests/second

Critics (my opinion, what I change in the code):
The String intern() method although is a good promise is a method that has an high cost (in another benchmark it is 20% of the CPU spent which is a lot).

The current version has mutable objects for the various objects:

* InternalQName
* JCRName
* JCRPath
* QPathEntry

The benefit of making them immutable are:

Reduce the creation cost of such objects.  For instance if you have a path that represents the value /a/b/c, when you want to create the parent path, the creation of the object is very fast as you do not have to copy the full object. A new object is created but reference the name array of the parent with a smaller size.
Allow efficient caching of the output of the methods like getAsString(). As the object is not mutable any more, the computed value of getAsString can be cached and does not need to be generated again when the method is invoked a second time

Moreover, it has some new and very useful features such as determining content types not only by file's extension, but also analyzing it's content.It is good configurable, it allows to exclude not necessary content handlers and add own ones as well

It supports out-of-the-box several kinds of metadata, such as: 
1. CreativeCommons up to 3 
2. DublinCore up to 16 
3. HttpHeaders up to 9 points
4. MSOffice up to 28 points

List of the content types supported by Tika is already longer that we support, it includes:
1. XML
2. Microsoft Office, including the Office OpenXML Format
3. HTML
4. RTF
5. PDF, including support of reading of the encrypted files
6. Text files
7. Open Office
8. Electronic Publication (EPUB)
9. Images (only metadata)
10. Archives (only metadata)
11. Java class
12. Audio files (only metadata)
13. Video files (only metadata)

Therefore I think it would be logical  to completely replace DocumentService with Apache Tika for document's content and metadata extracting

Below are my feelings about it after working with it for Generali customer.

Restoration over an existing workspace requires to delete data manually.
This should be managed by the service itself. I don't think leaving part of the procedure to manual work is acceptable.

If it not possible technically to do this by BackupManager himself (which I doubt), maybe we need to create an external tool handle the restore process fully (ie include drop db/fs data).

Restoration of system workspace is even worse because it requires to modify JCR configuration (set BackupWorkspaceInitializer).
In the past, there has been complaints because there was a need to modify configurations to enable clustering.

I fear we meet the same kind of concerns with the backup service. 
Backup is a must-have feature for EE, but our current implementaiton is not fully enteprise ready.

Please consider making backup more straightforward.

column279: 11/May/10 4:58 AM;nfilotto;Can't you use the character encoding provided by the ServletRequest http://java.sun.com/products/servlet/2.3/javadoc/javax/servlet/ServletRequest.html#getCharacterEncoding()?
column280:
13/May/10 5:07 AM;pnedonosko;WebDAV client usually doesn't provide an encoding.

How it works inside the eXo JCR indexer:
1. Indexer uses jcr:encoding property of nt:resource node (used as jcr:content child node of nt:file)
2. if no jcr:encoding property set the Document Service will use the one configured in the service (defaultEncoding)
3. if has nothing configured a JVM default encoding will be used

What we have in WebDAV - OS client (Windows, Linux etc) doesn't set an encoding in a request. 
But eXo JCR WebDAV server looks for an encoding in a Content-Type header and set it to jcr:encoding. See http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec14.html, 14.17 Content-Type. 
e.g. Content-Type: text/html; charset=ISO-8859-4
So, if a client will set Content-Type header, e.g. JS code from a page, it will works for a text file as expected.

If WebDAV request doesn't contain a content encoding it's possible to write a dedicated action in a customer application. The action will set jcr:encoding using its own logic, e.g. based on IP or user preferences.

column1: Reduce the concurrency Level in the JBoss Cache Config
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
Setting the concurrency level to 50000, consumes a lot of memory since it creates 50 000 segments per workspace. It should be reduced to 64. See below the initial email from Julien:

The memory consumption has been drastically reduced by decreasing the value concurrencyLevel from 50000 to 64.Initially I used the value 50000 initially by copying the JCR configuration without realizing the terrible consequences of using such high value. Basically the 50000 value was making the various ConcurrentHashMap of JBoss Cache consume around 1/2 (half) of the heap.
column277:
27/Apr/10 3:30 AM;nzamosenchuk;64 is critically small value for that. This means that JBC could handle 64 locks at the same time for the maximum. This will greatly reduce performance in multi-threading.
In few word, JBC makes hash from FQN, then finds the modulo by concurrency_level (  hash % concurrency_level  ) and this modulo is the index of lock in list (array?) of locks. So really, JBC places the lock not on FQN but on FQN-modulo-classes.  I.e. we have some 3 FQNs with hashes equals to: 64, 128, 196. When one is locked - others are locked also.
We can try/test reducing it, but not to 64. At least few hundreds. 
Also we should try lock stripping feature in JBC. It offers better performance and better memory usage without limiting the number of locks at the same time.
Lock stripping places the lock on concrete FQN but not on "class by modulo".
column278: 27/Apr/10 3:44 AM;nfilotto;if so you can remove it from the config since the default value is 500
column279:
28/Apr/10 3:54 AM;nzamosenchuk;1. LockStriping  led to deadlocks and "Unable to acquire lock". It's normal since even JBC documentation states this "deadlocks may occur". So LockStriping skipped.
2. Reducing Concurrency Level leads to great memory  freeing. 

Memory:
Just started JCR with Concurrency Level = 50000 (few times GC-ed) : 148M
Just started JCR with Concurrency Level = 500 (few times GC-ed) : 39M

Performance:
1. Daily on local machine are ok in ranges of statistic deviation, also waiting for QA approval.
2. AddNTFileWithMetadata benchmarks test within 800 threads and 30 iterations:

TPS per runs:
Concurrency Level = 50000 :  41.0;  40.4; 40.7
Concurrency Level = 500      :  39.4;  39.8; 40.3
So in general performance in this aggressive write test doesn't change.
3. Cluster tests in progress.

In general, this POC shows good results, much similar to original index implementation, some tests even show 3x increase, but some of them show decrease. The reason of decrease in absolutely unknown up to now and should be profiled.

* Single-Index currently has no RedoLog (comparing to trunk's version, have a RedoLog, that writes some bytes of data on FS, each time save() is called).


Also some aspects of NRT usage are now under investigation. They are:
* When commit is invoked and how can it be listened and/or controlled. 
* When optimize is called and how can it be controlled.
* Performance decrease in some tests.
* NRT interns and failover capabilities/external possibilities.
column285:
02/Jun/10 9:45 AM;nzamosenchuk;Lucene is not currently uses RAM directory internally. This is done only for 4.0 version (https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/LUCENE-1313). So currently segments are just only flushed from internal buffer on FS when reader is asked or some condition appears (this doesn't flush "deletes" on FS).
And even now, it shows adequate results in our tests.
This also means  that RedoLog should handle those flushes properly, cleaning up information of successfully flushed parts.

column1: Reuse WorkspaceStorageConnection via ThreadLocal storage
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column277:
19/Apr/10 4:56 AM;pnedonosko;ThreadLocal usage reviewed. Unfortunately it's not possible as we cannot link JCR Session to one Thread, i.e. several sessions can live in same thread or session can be used sequentially in several threads. At same time how to manage by a session close when it will be managed by GC. 

Such questions makes usage of connections pool more useful and controllable. 
With pool it will be possible to use once prepared statements (JDBC here) for several calls even in different threads.
To prevent a posible contention (most important disadvantage of pool) we can use self adopting algorithm without fixed threshold (max connections) or use soft threshold. Pool size can depends on configured "recommended" value of  maximum (depends on JDBC connections pool actually) and allowed  overload; use of available machine cores or memory can be taken in account also.
column278: 19/Apr/10 5:08 AM;nfilotto;I don't understand your comment, the idea of this JIRA is not to have one dedicated JCR Session per thread, it is to have one WorkspaceStorageConnection per Thread that will be shared between all JCR Sessions
column279:
19/Apr/10 6:25 AM;pnedonosko;Yes, I talk about one WorkspaceStorageConnection per Thread that will be shared between all JCR Sessions. 
We cannot share one WorkspaceStorageConnection between several active Sessions due to possible conflicts between not committed modifications in one and reads from another Session(s) - sessions should be isolated on persistent level.
We can share WorkspaceStorageConnection instance with only one Session at same time and it's independent on Thread this session runs in. There is benefit from WorkspaceStorageConnection instance reuse instead of recreation each time, but we cannot share WorkspaceStorageConnection between several concurrent calls in general case. In particular, WorkspaceStorageConnection can be a subject of share question for read only operations, I'll try to take it in account.
column280: 27/Apr/10 2:28 AM;pnedonosko;Only ThreadLocal based storage is not a solution due to arguments described above. But ThreadLocal variable still can be a case for pool implementation. Unfortunately it's not possible manage read only connections within a session performing saves. Further investigation will be done in parent issue.

25/Mar/10 7:45 AM;pnedonosko;The described error occurs when modification of already modifying content occurs, i.e. when you try to change the Item already changed in current save (observation it's a part of a save). So, the item (as part of XASession) will be locked by the save transaction until the save will not be finished.
This usecase is not actual for a standalone (non cluster) configuration where it's still possible to modify currently saving items. 
But with cluster configuration we have all JCR sessions (XA resource) joined to a XA transaction in Transaction service (JBossTransactionsService by default).

column1: Limit network traffic and thread blocking for the Lucene Indexer in a cluster
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47: We meet some issues of type "org.jboss.cache.lock.TimeoutException: Replication timeout" because we change the state of "index-update-in-progress" in JBC even when it is not necessary which causes a huge network traffic and blocks threads that should not be blocked. Indeed, in the Lucene Indexer, we have the notion of the Persisted Indexes and the Volatile Indexe, a thread in the coordinator need to be blocked when the Persisted Indexes and/or the Volatile Indexe are modified since they can all be accessed by this thread but, a thread in a node other than the coordinator is not aware of the Volatile Indexe so it should be only aware of any state change of the Persisted Indexes. In other words,  the state of "index-update-in-progress" in JBC should only be changed when the Volatile Index is flushed or the IndexMerger changes the list of indexes.

column1: Allow to reindex a workspace asynchronously
column11: This JIRA moved to http://jira.exoplatform.org/browse/JCR and is read-only.
column47:
When a JCR does not have any lucene, the indexation process is launch at startup, and this independently of the type of data/workspace/repository.

We should improve the process to make is smarter and avoid "blocking" entirely the system during the process that could be very long; depending of the size of the reposiroty.

Here a possible approach:

1- For each repository the administrator choose when the initial indexation process occurs: 
   1.1 - at startup like now, blocking the system until the repository is indexed
   1.2 - in a background proces, so the system has started and the indexation process occurs in a background process.

For 1.1: nothing new we keep it like what we have today
 - this will be configure for the various "system" repositories : Portal, DMS system, ...

For 1.2:
  - this will be configured for all "document" oriented repositories

  - during the indexation process the JCR should alert the application about its status, something like:
     "eXo JCR is currently being reindexed. Depending on how large the database is, this may take a few minutes. eXo will automatically become available as soon as this task is complete."
     "This process is 18% Completed."
 
 - during the process search will not be available but navigation by path should be.

 - we can provide an online tool to reindex the repository from an administration screen. (careful in case of clustering and big number of nodes)

column277:
02/Mar/10 9:13 AM;nzamosenchuk;Mentioned usecase is wrong. You possibly forget to remove node "/aaa/hello" before importing the history.

When You export version history for node "/aaa/hello" (i.e it's uuid is "11"), you really export version history for the node with this uuid ("11"). 
Then you are creating (importing) another node "/ccc/hello" (i.e. it's uuid will be "22") and then importing into it the history of another node (with uuid "11"). Because version history for it already exists, You got an exception. So you should remove node "/aaa/hello" (and so it's version history will be removed from version storage), before importing history. 

We'll add check for this case and more appropriate exception message.

Was expecting one of:
    <EOF> 
    "ORDER" ...
    "WHERE" ...
    "(" ...
    "," ...
So, why such exception is here? Parser expects some token from the list abouve, but got <identifier>-token. So some token is found but it is not acceptable by parser - this is parsing exception and parser may show in exception what it expects.

statement "select * from nt:base !where jcr:primaryType = 'nt:frozenNode'"
we have TokenMgrError with message
Lexical error at line 1, column 23.  Encountered: "!" (33), after : ""
Why suche error? There is no token definition for words beginnig with "!". So it's not a parser problem. 

And what is worse we can not use parser method where TokenMgrError was catched. That's why I use "Uncnown Query Construction". Because TokenMgrException may be catched in <literal> or <identifier> parser-method, but user uxpects that token is <comparisonOperator>

There is possible way to avoid TokenMgrExceptions at all
- make a garbage-token - token that accepts all unused chars and srings. So Lexer always may associate string or char with some token.  But such token is hard to implement.

column1: [jms] when using failover [re]connection attempts should stop upon non-temporary SASL failure
column47: When using a failover URI, the client continues to try and [re]connect upon encountering SASL failure for a given server. Realistically different servers in the failover list should behave similarly here, so continuing to attempt connection is likely to be futile and lead to a delay signalling the issue when the allowed attempts run out. When the SASL process fails with an outcome other than sys-temp, further [re]connection attempts should stop.

The FileLockNodeManager directory is always defaulted to the journal directory, but if it should be on a SAN/Geo-Replicated it means unwanted network resources and latencies.
It should be improved by allowing it to be configured in a local directory; making failover/startup faster.

column1: Deploy OpenShift cluster in OpenStack
column47:
This should help not just with migration of Cloud QE's testsuit, but also should help the other QE sub teams, that also need OpenShift cluster for testing.  I have been trying to deploy OpenShift in an OpenStack instance for a few days already, as well as some people from other QE sub teams.  Unfortunately they have been time restricted (other more immediate responsibilities and priorities) and I was unsuccessful so far. This task is to try to figure out solution for the issues described below.

We tried to deploy OpenShift cluster 3.10 on single node (per requirements form Kafka guys) on rhel 7.5 as recommended in documentation \[[1|https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.10/install/host_preparation.html]\] \[[2|https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.10/install/running_install.html#running-the-installation-playbooks]\]. Ansible role for installation failed for me in one of two ways:
* Unable to pull/read docker images (docker_image_availability check) - If that is first run of installation playbook, pulling images manually helps. if that is repeated iteration, only known solution (so far) is to start over with clean instance. Reboot doesn't help.

05/Dec/18 9:21 AM;gaohoward;[~clebert.suconic] What I observed is that the page cache was explicitly removed from soft map and the page file should be cleaned up at the point.
The problem is that the clean up happens in a very asynchronous way (one task delegated to another using executors). That makes harder to synchronize with transaction commits. When all messages in a page is done and ready to be clean up, some transaction operations (like RefsOperation.afterCommit()) are still on going and may access to the page cache (which probably all gone). 

My idea is to set some flags (either using some existing ones or new one if have to) to prevent the cache from being removed until all depending operations finish.

column1: LargeMessage Produced by AMQP Protocol Can Not Be Consumed By AMQP Protocol when consumer connected to different node
column47: When an AMQP consumer connects to a different node in AMQ 7 cluster then a AMQP producer large messages produced by the producer are never consumed.
column277: 05/Sep/18 3:51 AM;fnigro;[~clebert.suconic] ATM both AMQP and OpenWire don't have a full support of large messages, given that the messages are not sent/received in chunks: the customer behind this issue is using large messages + AMQP + clustering and I do believe that if we implement (in this sprint) the full support of large messages for AMQP any fix I will put for this issue will change, wasting effort. [~ataylor] [~martyn-taylor] Do we plan to fully support large messages on AMQP soon or I can proceed to find a temporary fix for this issue?
column278:
05/Sep/18 11:03 AM;fnigro;[~ataylor] Re "we only have a few days to finish this sprint": this issue isn't on the new sprint just started ie AMQ Broker 1836?
Anyway I think is fine to have a temp fix first (y)
column279: 06/Sep/18 9:07 AM;fnigro;While trying to reproduce it  I have found that the consumer is receiving a message that has its AMQP body not correctly converted.
column280:
07/Sep/18 4:10 AM;fnigro;After a further investigation it seems that when the message is crossing the bridge between nodes, on the receiver node it is converted into a NullStorageLargeServerMessage when no persistence is configured, making the whole read only body buffer to be just few bytes long.
the simplest fix seems to just expose the correct body buffer on NullStorageLargeServerMessage and extract the AMQPMessage from the embedded core message received.

column1: Store broker logs and related configuration files in CI jobs
column47:
Currently our CI jobs are hard to debug, because they do not contain any broker related debug files.

We miss broker.log. configuration files and possibly if OOM happens, we would like to store heap dump. 
In some cases, we might want to track heap-dumps (generated even N seconds/minutes) as well and store the as artifact of job.

Possible GC options:
{{-XX:+PrintGCApplicationStoppedTime -XX:+PrintGCTimeStamps -Xloggc:gc.log}}
Broker should be started with following to be able to generate thread dump on OOM:
{{-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError}}

column1: Openwire unable to receive larger message (10MB), but not "large"
column228: Given that the broker isn't supporting chunked large messages for both AMQP and OpenWire JMS clients, while using JMS consumer receive with timeout API is important to size properly the timeout according to the network bandwidth available betweeen clients and broker and the speed of the disk of the running broker, otherwise the timed receive won't be able to get the sent message in time.

10/Sep/18 9:55 AM;fnigro;I have created a test to reproduce it as well and with the latest master it isn't happening, but given the lack of support of large messages with OpenWire I'm not surprised (see https://issues.jboss.org/browse/ENTMQBR-1946).
I think that it is an issue per se (it largely depends on the memory available for both clients/server), but we have just 3 options for it:
* a complete fix that will deliver large message support to OpenWire (but ATM it seems not feasable)
* just document (if not) that the the protocol is not able to work with such large messages
* investigate to reduce some heavywieght & useless copies of the whole messages/data to reduce the chances bad things would happen

I would suggest the latter option, with the minimum dev effort possible here, but it is mostly dependent by our current needs and priority on this, [~ataylor]/[~martyn-taylor] seems reasonable?
column279:
11/Sep/18 8:54 AM;fnigro;I have taken a better look at the client used and I've noticed that when timeout == 0 it will call msgConsumer.receive(200) (ie 200 milliseconds) and then,
if no messages has been received, it will give up (indeed timeout = 0 has the correct semantic of "no waiting" or just wait a little in this case :P).

Given the size of the messages and the speed of OpenWire JMS client I have found that just using a blocking receive() or a higher enough timeout will solve the issue.

I suggest that improving docs to how use receive(timeout) warning about sizing properly timeout when AMQP or OpenWire and large messages are used would be a good thing.

column1: Native library libsnappyjava.so shipped with JBoss Fuse 6.1 is not compatible with RHEL 5 C++ runtime environment
column47:
Some components contains native library. For instance, camel-avro component needs to install this bundle:
{code}
org.apache.servicemix.bundles/org.apache.servicemix.bundles.snappy-java/1.0.4.1.redhat-001
{code}
and this bundle contains native library: libsnappyjava.so. 

Also the activemq-osgi bundle:
{code}
org.apache.activemq/activemq-osgi/5.9.0.redhat-610379
{code}
also contains the same native library. 

However, this native library is not compatible with RHEL5 C++ runtime environment. If you try to deploy it to a container that is running on a RHEL 5 machine, you will get following error:
{quote}
Caused by: java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: jboss-fuse-6.1.0.redhat-379/data/cache/bundle262/version0.0/bundle.jar-lib/0/org/xerial/snappy/native/Linux/amd64/libsnappyjava.so: /usr/lib64/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.9' not found (required by jboss-fuse-6.1.0.redhat-379/data/cache/bundle262/version0.0/bundle.jar-lib/0/org/xerial/snappy/native/Linux/amd64/libsnappyjava.so)
{quote}

Here is output from libsnappyjava.so lib:
{code}
jluo@rhel5_11$ strings org/xerial/snappy/native/Linux/amd64/libsnappyjava.so |grep GLIBC
GLIBC_2.4
GLIBC_2.2.5
GLIBCXX_3.4.9
GLIBCXX_3.4.11
GLIBCXX_3.4
{code}

And this is output from libstdc++.so.6 lib:
{code}
jluo@rhel5_11$ strings /usr/lib64/libstdc++.so.6 | grep GLIBC
GLIBCXX_3.4
GLIBCXX_3.4.1
GLIBCXX_3.4.2
GLIBCXX_3.4.3
GLIBCXX_3.4.4
GLIBCXX_3.4.5
GLIBCXX_3.4.6
GLIBCXX_3.4.7
GLIBCXX_3.4.8
GLIBC_2.3
GLIBC_2.3.2
GLIBC_2.4
GLIBC_2.2.5
GLIBCXX_FORCE_NEW
{code}

It's why the UnsatisfiedLinkError was thrown when trying to deploy these bundles.
column277:
06/Oct/14 1:09 PM;pgallagh;I replicated the problem and yes there is an incompatibility between the basic build/lib done on rhel6 then linked against a binary on rhel5.

Solutions :
1. Build snappy for the correct version of rhel (as that is the norm for c++ packages) 
  Pros - Guaranteed to work
  Cons - you would have to package multiple libs and the Java would have to work out which lib to load, or put the correct path in LD_LIBRARY_PATH before running
2. Build on rhel5 ONLY
Pros - the final linked binary either produced on rhel5 or re-linked on rhel6 against the libs built on rhel5 do work
Cons - would have to lock down all builds to rhel5 and not very future proff
3. Add option CXXFLAGS="-fabi-version=2" to the configure line in the spec file. (Preferred option)
Pros - works even if built on newer version of rhel so you can build on any version (rhel5,6 or 7) and then should work or re-link on any other. Easiest to do, just a change to the spec file

column1: AsyncWorkItemHandler documentation is incomplete
column47:
This handler is documented at two locations:
https://access.qa.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-jboss-bpm-suite/6.4/single/user-guide/#sect_multi_threading
https://access.qa.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-jboss-bpm-suite/6.4/single/development-guide/#job_executor_for_asynchronous_execution

Which is not ideal, and even after combining these two sections the documentation is not complete.

Q1: Are all parameters of this handler documented?
A1: See https://github.com/droolsjbpm/jbpm/blob/6.4.x/jbpm-services/jbpm-executor/src/main/java/org/jbpm/executor/impl/wih/AsyncWorkItemHandler.java#L36-#L54

Q2:  Is it necessary to create a work item with name "async" in order to use this handler?
A2: Nope. Work Item name is arbitrary. However, if the work item is named "async" then it's not necessary to register handler for it. It will be registered by default.

Q3: How to register this handler in the business-central?
A3: Using deployment descriptor, with this configuration:

{code:java}
<work-item-name>: new org.jbpm.executor.impl.wih.AsyncWorkItemHandler(org.jbpm.executor.ExecutorServiceFactory.newExecutorService(null))
{code}


Q4: How to correctly bring project with Command implementation on the classpath?
A4: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2709331

column47:
I found some issues when following the instructions from **12.3.2. Token-Based Authentication**:

1. For the 'kie-remote' client, the following instructions are incorrect and should thus be removed:
"Once you create a new client, its access value public by default. Change it to confidential"

4. {{echo RESULT}} needs to be changed to {{echo $RESULT}}

5. {{curl -H "Authorization: bearer TOKEN"}} needs to be changed to {{curl -H "Authorization: bearer $TOKEN"}}

In addition, the note at the end of 12.2.2 refers to a system property, but it is not described which system property. I assume it is {{org.kie.server.token}}, so this might need to be further explained as well.

column1: Does jBPM6 really authorize the Initiator,Stakeholder,Potential,Actual people to "nominate" a Task ?
column47:
Title: Task Permissions Matrix

Describe the issue:
- As per the "Table 12.2. Main Operations Permissions Matrix" from our BPMS 6.1 Development Guide [1] the people like "Initiator,Stakeholder,Potential,Actual" apart from Administrator can perform "nominate" operation on a Task.

- As per the WS-HT 1.1 specification [2] this is what it says about who can perform "nominate".
~~~
nominate: Task Initiator ("MAY" , it defines that vendor MAY chose to support the operation for the generic human role) , Business Administrator ("MUST" , it means that the operation MUST be available for the generic human role)
~~~

- I did some research on this matter quite sometime back for a support case and found that our jBPM6 code allows only BusinessAdministrator to perform "nominate" operation.

./jbpm-6.2.0.Final-redhat-4/jbpm-human-task/jbpm-human-task-core/src/main/resources/operations-dsl.mvel
~~~
...
	Operation.Nominate
    	: [ new OperationCommand().{
    			status = [ Status.Created ],
    			allowed = [ Allowed.BusinessAdministrator ],
    			exec = Operation.Nominate
    		} ], 
...
~~~

[1] https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-US/Red_Hat_JBoss_BPM_Suite/6.1/html/Development_Guide/sect-Task_Permissions.html#Task_Permissions_Matrix
[2] http://docs.oasis-open.org/bpel4people/ws-humantask-1.1-spec-cs-01.pdf

column1: BxMS 6.2 engine requires dependency on org.drools:drools-workbench-models-guided-dtable when using GuidedDecisionTables
column47:
Document URL: 

BRMS and BPMS Development Guide and Migration Guide

Describe the issue:

BxMS 6.2 introduces new requirement - when you build your own application embedding Drools/jBPM engine and you plan to process kJars which contain Guided Decision Tables, the engine needs to have the drools-workbench-models-guided-dtable jar on its classpath, otherwise loading of the kJar fails with ClassNotFoundException.

When using Maven, you can just declare the dependency by adding the following snippet into your <dependencies> section in pom.xml:

  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.drools</groupId>
    <artifactId>drools-workbench-models-guided-dtable</artifactId>
  </dependency>
 
Additional information: 

This is a difference from previous versions and it may confuse users who are not used to it - therefore, it should be highlighted in the docs.

Thanks!

column280:
23/Aug/16 8:58 AM;marek.winkler;Hi [~vidya_iyengar],

there are differences:
- {{org.drools:drools-workbench-models-guided-dtable}} is required when you want to work with *guided* decision tables, i.e. Decision tables created by Business central _Guided Decision Table editor_, the file extension of this kind of assets is {{.gdst}}. On the other hand, 
{{org.drools:drools-decisiontables}} is used for Decision tables (not "guided") either in {{.csv}} or {{.xls}} format.

- another difference is the situation what you want to do, you may want either to:
  -- just *compile* a kjar containing assets of that type - for this scenario, using {{kie-maven-plugin}} is preferred, as you correctly mentioned,
  -- *use* (i.e. load by Drools runtime) an already compiled kjar containing assets of that type (or compile the kjar on-the-fly by using programmatic API and then load it by Drools runtime) - this scenario is not covered by {{kie-maven-plugin}}, therefore users would have to add the required dependencies on the classpath so Drools runtime can load them. This JIRA is aimed to describe this type of scenario.

To provide more context, this JIRA is targeted to the "embedded" use-case (i.e. when you embed the Drools/jBPM engine in your own application). When you want to use a kjar in KIE-server, you do not need to add those dependencies, since KIE-server itself already has them.

Hope this helps!

column1: Allow to override dependency when importing AeroGear Services IOS SDK
column11: Mobile Services
column47:
h4. Motivation 

SDK can depend on external dependencies like alamofire. 
Alamofire is really popular networking library and it may be used in the user application.
Having two different versions of the same library will cause conflict on build.
Users will need to change their version to comply with our version, which is not acceptable aproach.



This problem is really well described and mentioned in many bugs. 
For example:
https://github.com/CocoaPods/CocoaPods/issues/461

We will need to figure out solution the same as we done on Android when we decided to use BOM version management.

h4. How

We need to replicate the same work we have done for Android by allowing developers to avoid dependency problems or document how to handle that situations.
column277: 01/Feb/18 12:09 PM;wtrocki;After talk with [~danielpassos] we agreed that we cannot ignore that issue as this will be huge limitation for the SDK developers.
column278:
09/Feb/18 6:03 AM;wtrocki;Initial investigation finished:
Common solution is to provide wide version range for dependencies - never fixed version as this will cause conflicts for others.

However we cannot really say and test many use cases as our modules are now linked as development pods:
!Screen Shot 2018-01-29 at 2.31.54 PM.png|thumbnail! 

When conflict happens it's it's usually because invalid version ranges:
{code}
[!] CocoaPods could not find compatible versions for pod "Alamofire":
  In Podfile:
    AGSCore (from `../modules/core`) was resolved to 1.0.0, which depends on
      Alamofire (= 4.6.0)

    Alamofire (< 4.5)
{code}

Going to adjust ranges in PR.

h6. What
We should verify that the access token was signed using the Keycloak realm that it originated from to prevent tampering on the client side.

h6. Why
To prevent the possibility of a malicious user tampering with the access token to add additional roles to attempt to bypass some access control checks in the mobile app.

h6. How
This should be called before carrying out access control decisions within the app (It can probably be part of the getRoles function in [AGDROID-684|https://issues.jboss.org/browse/AGDROID-684]). This function should confirm that the Access token was signed using the realm that the client interact's with. The public key of the realm can probably be hard coded in the application and used for digital signature checks. 

The issuer can be matched too - http://localhost:8080/auth/realms/MY_REALM to the issuer of the JWT. 

Perhaps there can be a verifyToken() and a verifyIssuer()

*Note*: This probably doesn't need to be exposed by the SDK. Its probably just an additional check to perform.

column1: make a decision on how we want to deliver the SDK for the IDM service
column11: Mobile Services
column47:
h1. Why

In order to implement the SDK for the IDM service, there are a few options. We need to make a decision on which approach we will take. 

h1. What

Options to consider are:

* Option 1 - Use an existing 3rd party implementation
** Pros
*** Small amount of work required.
*** Opportunity to contribute to the open source project
** Cons
*** No control over the priority of feature delivery
*  Option 2 - Create our own SDK, but it will depends on an existing 3rd party implementation
** Pros
*** Relatively less amount of work
*** Full control of the features
*** Can change 3rd party lib without impact on the users
** Cons
*** Need to make sure the user's app is not using a conflicting 3rd party lib
* Option 3 - Eat our own dog food
** Pros
*** Full control of the features
*** No dependency on 3rd party lib
*** Fully target towards our own usecase
** Cons
*** A lot of work
*** Potentially re-invent the wheel?

The decision from this should apply for all the service SDKs, not only just the IDM service SDK.

h2.  How

Create a proposal to https://github.com/aerogear/proposals/pull/8 and recommend option 2.

The 3rd party library we are going to use is AppAuth:
https://github.com/openid/AppAuth-android

column1: dynamic load the public key in order to verify the token
column11: Mobile Services
column47:
*What*

We have implemented token integrity check as part of AGDROID-686. The implementation is based on the assumption that the public key of the realm will be available from mobile-services.json file.

However, based on the research and this SO issue (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40503697/keycloak-missing-realm-public-key), it is not recommended to hard code the realm public key into the configuration file as the admin user could rotate it in KC to improve security. We need to add support for that.

*How*

The proposed approach is this:

* check if there is a `realm-public-key` in the config file for keycloak. If there is, use it.
* If there isn't such value, load it dynamically
** After a successful login, first check if there is a cached version of the public key. If there is, check if the cached key is still valid (there should a configurable value to specify how long a public key can be valid locally)
** If there is no such cached key, or if the cached key is invalid, load it from the backend (use '/openid-connect/cert' endpoint). Save it in the local cache.

column1: Improve and document container-based workflow for the Metrics API server
column11: Mobile Services

h3. Why
Running the Metrics API locally for development and integration tests will require a database available, and supplying an easy way for contributors to run it alongside a containerized build of the project can offer some benefits:

- Allow running of the project without requiring setup of a golang dev environment
- Making builds reproducible by enforcing golang version
- Help generate a container image for the APB targetting openshift

h3. How
Currently the repo has a set of container configs in the deployments/ directory

These can be improved by:
- Utilizing the same make-based commands for compiling the project
- Utilizing multi-stage builds to generate a smaller final image
- Allowing the user to easily run the containerized database and metrics api project in any combination for development and testing purposes
- Add a separate configuration file for building an image on top of the official release binaries

The implementation would build on top of ideas spiked in the following closed PRs for the project repo:

- https://github.com/aerogear/aerogear-metrics-api/pull/11

*What*
Document the required & optional bits for a service APB.
The target for this document is a an APB developer that want's the provisioned service to be consumable as a 'Mobile Service'
(see terminology https://github.com/aerogear/mobile-core/blob/master/docs/architecture/architecture-overview.adoc#terminology)

*Why*
So an APB developer knows what is required to be able to integrate with the Mobile CLI and SDKs.
Also, so an APB developer knows what optional integrations & configuration there are e.g. Prometheus metrics endpoint via annotations

*How*

This list is not exhaustive, but a starting point. There may be other requirements and optional bits that would benefit from being documented.
*See comment thread for additional considerations*

Required
* Split of Configmap & Secret for any config/keys to be exposed to Mobile apps vs. 'administrative' secrets. See https://github.com/aerogear/proposals/blob/master/apbs/create-secret-and-configmap-during-provision.md
* Use Kuberentes Resources as much as possible (rather than OpenShift Resources). e.g. use a Deployment instead of a DeploymentConfig. This is to ensure compatibility with both Kubernetes & OpenShift.

Optional
* Metrics endpoint for Prometheus. See https://github.com/aerogearcatalog/metrics-apb/blob/master/roles/provision-metrics-apb/templates/prometheus-config-map.yml.j2
* Metrics dashboard for Grafana. See https://github.com/aerogearcatalog/metrics-apb#how-auto-discovery-of-services-work

Questions:
* Are there considerations for a 'shared service'? https://github.com/aerogear/proposals/blob/master/apbs/use-shared-services-across-namespaces.md
* Are there considerations for a integrating with another service?
